The most recent refreshes, newest first (take 1 to 100, default 20)

The baskets with their member counts: the system baskets first (kind portfolio: one per portfolio bucket, read-only, by account then name), then the owner's in their order (kind manual); archived manual ones only with includeArchived=true

post.summary: Create an empty basket (name, colour, purpose, description); 409 baskets.name_taken when an active basket has the name (ignoring case)

put.summary: Put the baskets in this order: the ids must be every active basket exactly once (400 baskets.invalid), 409 baskets.conflict when baskets changed meanwhile

post.summary: Copy or move up to 500 instruments from one basket to another, atomically and idempotently (only members of the source are transferred; targets are tracked automatically); a system basket can be the source of a copy only, anything else with one is 409 baskets.system

put.summary: Replace the name, colour, purpose and description of a basket that is not archived; 409 baskets.system for a system basket

delete.summary: Archive a basket (idempotent): it leaves the list, its members and history stay readable, instruments stay tracked; 409 baskets.system for a system basket

get.summary: The members of a basket in their order, with the instrument and its tracked block; asOf=yyyy-MM-dd (India date) gives the members at the end of that day. A system basket gives the instruments of the bucket's current holdings with quantity and accountName; asOf on it is 400 baskets.invalid

post.summary: Add 1 to 500 instruments (idempotent, all or nothing); untracked ones are tracked in the same transaction, a retired one that is not tracked is refused (instruments.retired)

delete.summary: Remove 1 to 500 instruments (idempotent, all or nothing); the stay stays in the history, the instruments stay tracked

put.summary: Put the members in this order: the instrumentIds must be every member exactly once (400 baskets.invalid), 409 baskets.conflict when the basket changed meanwhile

get.summary: The newest additions and removals of a basket, newest first (take 1 to 1000, default 200); 400 baskets.invalid for a system basket
The baskets (not archived) that hold the instrument now

Holdings with lots summary, profit/loss, XIRR and day change: accountId, bucketId, status (open default, closed, all), q (symbol, name, ISIN), sort (symbol, name, qty, avgCost, lastPrice, invested, value, pnl, pnlPct, xirr, dividends, dayChange, dayChangePct, acquiredOn, bucket, account; prefix - for descending; rows without a value last), page, pageSize (max 100), groupBy (account, bucket, sector, basket) with groupKey (account id, bucket id, sector name, basket id, or ~none for Unclassified / No basket) to list one group's holdings; an unknown key gives an empty page. With groupBy and no accountId only accounts that count in totals are listed (includeInTotals), like the groups and the summary, while the list without groupBy includes the others too. Each row has previousClose, dayChange (rupees), dayChangePct (percent), priceAt and priceSource (sync, quote or live) and income (null when the holding has no dividend and no trade charge recorded): dividends, charges (trade charges), totalReturnPct = (realised + unrealised + dividends) over invested, netTotalReturnPct (minus the charges), netXirr with netXirrState, and the dates coverageFrom, dividendsFrom and chargesFrom the figures are known from

Totals of the holdings of an account or bucket (all accounts that count in totals when neither is given): invested, value, P&L, XIRR, day change (dayChange, dayChangePct, dayChangeExcluded: open holdings left out for lack of a previous close), counts, lots on the default date, pricesAsOf (oldest and newest price time), last sync. income (null when nothing is recorded): dividends, charges, unallocated (dividends of no holding), totalReturnPct, netTotalReturnPct, netXirr and netXirrState, coverageFrom / dividendsFrom / chargesFrom; for the portfolio or an account (no bucket) it includes the dividends of no holding and the ledger's costs, for a bucket only its holdings'. benchmarkXirr and alpha stay price returns, before dividends and charges

The holdings grouped by account, bucket, sector or basket (by): per group holdings, unpriced, invested, value, P&L (rupees and percent), realised, XIRR (from the union of the group's cash flows) and xirrState, day change, dayChangeExcluded and weightPct (share of the scope's total value), plus the scope total; additive is false for baskets (a holding is in every live basket that holds it, or in No basket; groups overlap). Filters: accountId, bucketId, status (open default, closed, all), q; sort (value, invested, pnl, pnlPct, xirr, dividends, dayChange, name; prefix - for descending; default largest value first; groups without a value last; at most 200 groups). stackBy (account when by=sector, sector when by=account) adds parts[{key, name, value}] to each group. Group keys: account id, bucket id, sector name, basket id, ~none for Unclassified / No basket (a master sector spelled ~none counts as Unclassified). Without accountId only accounts that count in totals (includeInTotals) are in the groups, the total and the children, unlike the flat holdings list which includes the others; an unknown accountId gives 200 with no groups (not 404 as for the summary); more than 200 groups are cut off without a flag, the total still covers the whole scope. A group of only unpriced holdings, and a total of only unpriced holdings, have null value, pnl, pnlPct, xirr and xirrState no_price (the summary shows value 0). Each group and the total have income (null when nothing is recorded; see the summary): a group by account also holds the account's dividends of no holding and its ledger costs; the dividends and costs of no group are in the total and in an extra last group with the key ~unallocated (name Unallocated, no holdings, no value, xirrState no_data) - only when no bucket and no q narrows the scope
The lots of a holding with the profit/loss and XIRR of each

put.summary: Set the acquisition date of a lot (1990-01-01 to today); the lot stops using the default date. A lot rebuilt from trades (source trade) takes its date from the trade: 409 portfolio.lot_from_trade; the opening lot of such a holding must stay before the earliest trade: 400 portfolio.invalid, field acquiredOn

post.summary: Fetch the account's holdings from Dhan for the first import in the portfolio settings, saving nothing; defaultDate (and each row's suggestedDate) is the account's first import date, 2025-01-01 until the owner chooses another

Sync now: bring the holdings in line with Dhan (an account without holdings is imported instead, every holding dated with its first import date and the run recorded as an import; new holdings dated today, quantity changes as lots, sales closed first-in first-out); optional body {confirm, expectedOpenHoldings, expectedWouldClose}; 409 portfolio.sync_running while a sync runs; 409 portfolio.confirmation_required (listedHoldings, openHoldings, wouldClose) when Dhan's answer would close all or most holdings, unless confirm is true with the numbers echoed back; 409 portfolio.confirmation_stale when the answer differs from the confirmed numbers

get.summary: The account's refresh settings (mode, daily time, first import date, hasHoldings), the next scheduled run and the latest sync run, and its health (ADR 0027): consecutiveFailedDays (days in a row whose last attempt failed; 0 when the latest succeeded), lastFailureReason (unavailable, rate_limited, interrupted, rejected, token_expired, token_refused, not_connected, data_changed, unexpected; null while healthy), attempts (failed attempts of the day of the latest failure) and retryAt (when the next quiet retry is due; null when none is pending - a failure that may pass is retried after 1, 5 and 15 minutes inside the day and nothing is shown while retries remain)

Value history of the lots of a scope (accountId, bucketId; all accounts that count in totals when neither is given) from the lots and the stored day bars adjusted for splits and bonuses: points {date, value, invested, benchmarkValue (the same cash flows in the benchmark index, null when unavailable), nav, benchmarkNav} (NAV starts at 100 and ignores cash flows), coverage {holdings, covered, unpriced, lateStart}, partial, benchmark {state ok|unavailable, instrumentId, symbol, name, tracked, hasBars, reason}, maxDrawdown and benchmarkMaxDrawdown {pct, from, to} (a fall of pct %), firstDate, lastPriceAt (set when the last point is today's live one) and resolution. from/to yyyy-MM-dd; resolution day|week|month (last trading day of the period; default the finest with at most 2,000 points, 400 portfolio.invalid when a given one gives more). An unknown account or bucket gives an empty history

The benchmark index the portfolio is compared with (Nifty 50 until another is chosen): instrumentId, symbol, name, isDefault, tracked, hasBars; all null when the instrument master has no such index yet

put.summary: Choose the benchmark index: body {instrumentId} of any index of the instrument master that is still listed; 400 portfolio.invalid for no id, an unknown id, a non-index or a retired index. Audited; the cached histories are dropped

post.summary: Track my holdings: tracks the instruments of the open holdings of the scope (accountId, bucketId) that are in the instrument master, with the bulk tracking command; idempotent. Answers how many were added, how many holdings are not in the master (notInMaster) and how many instruments are retired and skipped; starts no job, the hint says the next Update data builds the bars

Track the benchmark: tracks the benchmark index with the bulk tracking command; idempotent. Answers how many were added; starts no job, the hint says the next Update data builds the bars. 404 portfolio.not_found when the instrument master has no benchmark index

get.summary: The CSV folder (files loaded and pending), the Dhan Data account and whether a fetch can run, the aggregates per timeframe, the stored bars with the last bar (last tick) and how many trading days (by the trading calendar) it is behind, the job in progress, the last job of each phase, the next holiday, how many calendar days await confirmation, the gaps in the bars (open, unfillable, filled), the scheduled end-of-day run (enabled, time, next run, last automatic run) and pendingCorporateActions (suggested splits or bonus issues waiting for a decision)

The tracked instruments and the ones with bars, with first bar, last bar, 1-minute bars, source (csv|dhan|mixed), status (current|behind|empty) and the open gaps: q, status, hasGaps (true keeps instruments with open gaps), sort (symbol|name|firstBar|lastBar|bars, '-' for descending), page, pageSize (max 200)

The latest bars of an instrument, newest first: timeframe 1m|5m|10m|15m|30m|1h|1D|1W|1M (default 1D), take 1 to 1000 (default 100), adjusted (default false = raw prices; true adjusts prices and volume for the applied corporate actions on read — each bar by the factor of its India date, a week or month bar by the first day of its bucket — and adds the adjustment block: applied, factor, actions)

post.summary: Start a data update in the background: steps (any of csv, dhan, aggregate, quality; default csv, dhan and aggregate, always in that order; quality checks the data after the others, see /data/quality), forceCsv loads unchanged CSV files again, refetchGaps also retries the sessions the Dhan phase gave up on (unfillable), csvFiles (1 to 214 file names of the CSV folder, only with the csv step; see /data/csv/files) loads only those files - an empty list or a name the folder does not have is 400 data.invalid naming it. 202 with the job; 409 data.job_running while one runs, 409 data.master_missing without an instrument list

get.summary: The most recent data updates, newest first (take 1 to 100, default 20)
The sessions of tracked instruments with missing 1-minute bars (ADR 0017 §3), newest first: status (open|filled|unfillable), instrumentId, page, pageSize (max 200)

What the owner should know about the data for the notification bell: sessions with missing bars (data_gaps_open), instruments failing the data quality checks (data_quality_failed), suggested corporate actions to review (data_corporate_actions_pending). A failed scheduled run is no longer here: it is the service_failed notice of GET /api/services/notices

The trading calendar: confirmed holidays and special sessions from..to (yyyy-MM-dd, default today and a year on, at most 3660 days), every proposed day (from the stored bars, also a proposal next to a confirmed day: replaces names that day's kind) and the next holiday

post.summary: Add a holiday (a weekday) or a special session (sessionFrom/sessionTo HH:mm India time; both left out means 09:15 to 15:30) as confirmed, replacing what the date had. 201 for a new date, 200 when it replaced a row; 400 data.invalid with the field
Read NSE's public holiday list now (best effort, one request). Always 200: succeeded=false with the reason when NSE refused or the list could not be read; add holidays by hand then

put.summary: Confirm a proposed day (idempotent; a proposal next to a confirmed day replaces it); 404 data.calendar_day_not_found when the date has no row or was dismissed, 400 data.invalid for a date that cannot be read

delete.summary: Take a day off the calendar, or dismiss a proposal: the owner's own entry is deleted; a proposal from the stored bars or a day from NSE's list stays as dismissed so it is not proposed again (removing a dismissed day deletes it); a date with a proposal next to a confirmed day dismisses only the proposal (remove again to take the day off). 204; 404 data.calendar_day_not_found

get.summary: One data update with the progress and result of each phase
The latest run over every instrument, the counts (checked, passed, warnings, failed, never checked) and the mean score of the current results, the gate, the window of sessions and the limits in force

The tracked instruments with bars and the current result of their checks: q, status (pass|warning|fail|notChecked), sort (symbol|name|status|score|coverage|barsChecked|missingMinutes|checkedAt, '-' for descending), page, pageSize (max 200)

Every check of one instrument, its missing minutes (at most 500 listed, with the total) and the stored buckets of the window next to the ones recomputed from the 1-minute bars now: differencesOnly, timeframe (5m|10m|15m|30m|1h|1D|1W|1M)
The most recent quality runs, newest first (take 1 to 100, default 20)

The fail-closed gate for the nightly plan: blocked when no finished run exists, the last finished run failed or is older than 3 trading days, or more than Data:Quality:MaxFailedPercent of the checked instruments fail (a running run is no verdict); ok when not blocked and none fails; reasons say why

post.summary: Run the checks in the background (a data job with the step quality): instrumentId limits it to one instrument. 202 with the job; 409 data.job_running while any data job runs, 404 data.instrument_not_found

Fix action: fetch the instrument's missing bars from Dhan again (gap days, including unfillable ones), rebuild its aggregates and check it again, as one data job. 202 with the job; 409 data.job_running, data.dhan_not_connected or data.dhan_not_available; 404 data.instrument_not_found

Fix action: rebuild the instrument's derived timeframes over the window from its 1-minute bars and check it again, as one data job. 202 with the job; 409 data.job_running; 404 data.instrument_not_found

get.summary: The files of the CSV folder: state (pending|loaded|changed - loaded, but size or modified time differ now), size, modified time, the symbol parsed from the name, the instrument it maps to or why not (unknown|ambiguous|invalidName), and rows, firstBar, lastBar, loadedAt and overlapsWith (other loaded files of the instrument covering part of the same time) for loaded files. No file is opened, so hundreds of files list at once. Changed and pending first, then loaded, by name: q (name or symbol), state, page, pageSize (max 200)

post.summary: Dry run of the real reader, row rules and session check over up to 20 files of the folder (names from the listing; anything else is that file's error), nothing written: rows, first and last bar, trading days, repaired and rejected with up to 10 examples, the verdict (pass or the refusal message), the symbol mapping, the first 5 accepted rows and what loading would do to the stored bars (would insert, update, keep existing Dhan bars, unchanged; a spread sample past 1 million lookups per request, flagged sampled). A request reads at most 2 times the per-file limits of Data:Csv and works for at most 60 seconds

Undo the load of one CSV file as a data job: removes the file's csv-source bars of its instrument within the file's recorded first-to-last bar (Dhan bars stay), makes the file pending again, then rebuilds the instrument's aggregates; audited. Values an earlier load overwrote are NOT restored (no history is kept). The removal is by instrument and range: bars of another loaded file in the overlap go too, and the job warns. 202 with the job; 409 data.job_running while any data job runs; 404 data.csv_file_not_found when the file was never loaded

get.summary: The splits and bonus issues, newest ex-date first: status (suggested|applied|ignored), instrumentId, page, pageSize (max 200); pending is the number of suggestions waiting, whatever the filter

post.summary: Add a split (numerator:denominator = old shares : new shares, 1:5 gives a factor of 0.2) or a bonus (bonus shares : shares held, 1:1 gives 0.5) as applied. 201; 400 data.invalid with the field; 404 data.instrument_not_found; 409 data.corporate_action_exists, 409 data.corporate_action_conflicts_same_day (an applied action of the other kind is on that ex-date), 409 data.csv_already_adjusted (the ex-date is on or before csvAdjustedThrough: the loaded CSV files are adjusted at source; send acknowledgeCsvAdjusted=true, in the body or the query, to add it anyway)

put.summary: Confirm a suggestion (an empty body confirms it as it is), change the ex-date, kind, ratio or note, or bring back an ignored action: the result is applied. Fields left out keep their value. 200; 400 data.invalid; 404 data.corporate_action_not_found; 409 data.corporate_action_exists, 409 data.corporate_action_conflicts_same_day, 409 data.csv_already_adjusted (as when adding; acknowledgeCsvAdjusted=true in the body or the query)

post.summary: Decline an action: it stays in the list as ignored (nothing is deleted) and is not suggested again. Idempotent. 200; 404 data.corporate_action_not_found
Look for splits and bonus issues in the stored day bars of every share and ETF now; new candidates become suggested actions, nothing is applied and repeating it finds nothing new. 200 with the counts

Import actions from CSV (header symbol,exDate,kind,numerator,denominator; RELIANCE or NSE:RELIANCE; at most 5,000 lines) sent as the text/csv or text/plain body, or as the first file of a multipart/form-data upload; they are applied. preview=true writes nothing and returns the counts. Unknown symbols are listed, never guessed; duplicates (any status) are skipped; bad lines (also a kind that clashes with an applied one on the same day) are reported and skipped. Lines with an ex-date on or before the date the loaded CSV files reach (adjusted at source) are counted in adjustsCsvTwice and listed in warnings; importing them needs acknowledgeCsvAdjusted=true. 200; 400 data.invalid; 409 data.csv_already_adjusted (with adjustsCsvTwice and instruments)

get.summary: Every registered service (id, name, description, runsAs, enabled, schedule with words, execution settings, parameters with their schema, status healthy|running|failed|paused, lastRun, nextRun, issues, isDefault, revision) and the read-only entries (the per-account sync: readOnly true, manageUrl /accounts)

The trading-day timeline of a date (date yyyy-MM-dd, India time; default today): market hours, the review cutoff, whether it is a trading day and the starts (marks) and up-times (bands) of every enabled service, with the service a run-after entry follows

What the owner should know about the services for the notification bell: service_failed for the latest run of each service with notify on failure when it failed and no retry follows (id service:failed:{serviceId}:{yyyy-MM-dd}: one notice per service per India day, text and time of the latest failure); the next run of the service clears it
One service as the list shows it. 404 services.not_found

The runs and attempts of a service, newest first (page from 1, pageSize 1 to 100, default 25; the latest 200 are shown). trigger scheduled|catch_up|after|manual, status running|succeeded|failed|skipped, dataJobId links the data job a run started. 404 services.not_found

put.summary: Save enabled, schedule (type daily|weekly|after|window|interval|continuous with its fields, times HH:mm India time), retries 0-5, timeoutMinutes 1-240, catchUp, notifyOnFailure and parameters, with the revision read. Checked against all services: 400 services.invalid with issues[] (service, field, message) when anything is wrong, nothing stored; warnings come back with the service. 409 services.revision_changed on a stale revision, 404 services.not_found, 409 services.read_only. Takes effect at the next look of the scheduler, no restart

post.summary: Dry run of a save: the same checks (issues: errors and warnings) and the next three starts, nothing stored. The revision is not looked at. 404 services.not_found, 409 services.read_only

Restore default: writes the definition's default choices (nothing is deleted). Audited. 400 services.invalid if they would break a rule against the other services, 404 services.not_found, 409 services.read_only
Pause: no scheduled, catch-up or run-after starts; past times are not made up for when it is resumed; Run now still works. Audited. 404 services.not_found, 409 services.read_only
Resume a paused service. Audited. 404 services.not_found, 409 services.read_only

Run now (trigger manual), also for a paused service. 202 with the run, which goes on in the background (for the end-of-day run its dataJobId links the data job whose progress /api/data/jobs/{id} shows). For the live feed, which another container runs, nothing starts here: the request is audited, the manual-run marker is written (Live:ManualRunMinutes, default 30) and the answer is a run with status queued and an empty id (the feed opens its run record within 15 seconds). Audited. 409 services.already_running when it runs (a skipped run is recorded), 404 services.not_found, 409 services.read_only

get.summary: The holdings that need a decision, evaluated on read by seven rules (below_cost, large_gain, overweight, sector_concentration, long_term_soon, lagging_nifty, not_in_basket): items[{id, rule, severity high|medium|info, accountId, accountName, holdingId, instrumentId, symbol (null for the account-level sector_concentration), title, detail, numbers (the figures behind the item; which are set depends on the rule), suggestions[open|set_alert|add_to_basket|snooze|done], state open|snoozed|done, snoozedUntil}] most important first (severity, then the size of the trigger), and counts {open, snoozed, done, byRule, bySeverity (of the open items; every rule and severity present), unavailable {lagging: holdings held long enough for lagging_nifty that could not be judged because the benchmark has no bars from the first flow or an XIRR is not ok}, noPrice (open holdings without a usable price: no price-based rule fires for them)}. Filters: accountId (404 accounts.not_found when unknown; without it the accounts that count in totals), bucketId (the items about its holdings; weights and sector shares stay shares of the whole account), status open (default) | snoozed | done | all (the counts always cover the whole scope). A snoozed item shows again on its snoozedUntil date. One write is made by this read: a done decision whose condition no longer holds is cleared, so a recurrence shows again

post.summary: Hide an item for 7 days (it shows again on that India date if a rule still produces it): answers {id, state, snoozedUntil, item}. Idempotent; audited. 404 portfolio.not_found for an id that no rule produces now (stale)

Mark an item done: it stays hidden for as long as the condition holds and the decision is cleared when it stops holding (a later recurrence is open again). Answers {id, state, snoozedUntil, item}. Idempotent; audited. 404 portfolio.not_found for an id that no rule produces now (stale)

Take a snooze or done decision back: the item is open again. Answers {id, state open, item (null when no rule produces the id now)}. Idempotent; audited when it changes something; allowed for an item that is gone; 404 portfolio.not_found only for an id that is not the id of any rule's item

get.summary: The thresholds of the Action-center rules in force: values {belowCostPct, belowCostHighPct, gainPct, overweightFloorPct, overweightMultiple, minPositions, concentrationPct, lagPp, lagDays, longTermWindowDays}, the documented defaults, isDefault, updatedBy and updatedAt (null while none are stored)

put.summary: Save the thresholds (all ten required): below cost 1-90 %, high 2-95 % and above below cost, gain 1-1000 %, overweight floor 1-100 %, multiple 1-10, minimum positions 2-50, concentration 5-100 %, lag 1-100 points, lag days 30-3650, long-term window 1-365 days; at most 2 decimals, minPositions/lagDays/longTermWindowDays whole numbers. 400 portfolio.invalid with a field error per problem. The next read of the actions uses them at once. Audited

post.summary: Restore defaults: writes the documented default thresholds. Audited; nothing changes when they are already in force

get.summary: What the owner should know about the portfolio, for the notification bell. Every item has id, kind, severity, text, at, title, actions (at most two: {label, kind route|command, target}), since and resolved; alertId, instrumentId and accountId are set where they apply. Kinds: price_alert_triggered (warn; one per alert, id portfolio:alert:{alertId}, listed for 7 days after it triggered) and actions_need_decision (info; "N holdings need a decision" when the accounts that count in totals have open Action-center items; id portfolio:actions:{India date}, so it is raised again at most once a day) and, since ADR 0027, the attention items derived from the state of the accounts and syncs: reconnect_dhan (the Dhan login is missing, expired or about to expire), sync_failing (holdings, trades, ledger or prices failing on 2 days in a row, or at once when only the owner can fix it; never while a quiet retry is still to come), holdings_need_review (hand-dated lots), trades_unexplained (a quantity the trades do not explain once earlier history cannot help), dividends_pending (ledger credits that look like dividends) and securities_unmatched (no instrument-master match). Their severity is error, warning or info (the older kinds say warn/info), their id includes the situation (a changed situation is a new item), and a route action's target is an in-app path while a command action's target is an existing endpoint as METHOD /api/path. An item whose condition stopped holding stays for 24 hours with resolved true and is then dropped; resolved items are not counted in the badge. Order: unresolved before resolved, error, warning, info, newest first. This read remembers the items it derives (a set-based write; nothing is deleted)

The price alerts, newest first: status active | triggered | cancelled | all (default all), page, pageSize (max 100, default 50). Each alert has id, instrumentId, symbol, name, direction (at_or_below | at_or_above), level, note, status, createdAt, triggeredAt and triggerPrice (the last price of the tick that hit the level). The page also carries activeCount of activeLimit (200)

post.summary: Create an active alert: body {instrumentId (an NSE share or ETF of the instrument master that is not retired and that Dhan can quote), direction at_or_below | at_or_above, level (above 0, at most 10,000,000, at most 4 decimals), note (optional, at most 200 characters of plain text)}. Checked on each quotes tick's last price (at_or_below: last <= level; at_or_above: last >= level). 400 portfolio.invalid with field errors, including field level when the condition already holds at the last known price (the holding's last price, else the last stored daily close; unknown: allowed) with the price in the message; 409 portfolio.alert_limit at 200 active alerts. Audited

Cancel an alert. Idempotent: a cancelled alert stays cancelled and a triggered one stays triggered (the answer shows the real status). Audited when it cancels. 404 portfolio.not_found for an unknown id

get.summary: The template of a tradebook file as a CSV download: the canonical header (Date, Symbol, ISIN, Side, Quantity, Price, Exchange, Trade ID, Time, Charges) and two example rows. Other header names are accepted too (any case, punctuation ignored); only date, symbol or ISIN, side, quantity and price are required

post.summary: Read a tradebook against an account and say what importing it would do, storing and changing nothing. Body: multipart/form-data with accountId (an account with the Portfolio role) and file (CSV, UTF-8, at most 10 MB and 20,000 data rows). Returns the file (rows, parsed, skipped by reason, bad rows with line and reason - at most 200 listed, badTotal counts all -, duplicates, alreadyImported, newTrades), the securities - every held or master-listed one and at most 200 unmatched ones; securitiesTotal counts all, unmatchedListed the unmatched listed - (symbol, isin, matched, holdingId, trades, buys, sells, first and last trade date and the rebuild: status ok | unchanged | quantity_mismatch | no_holding | ambiguous, reason, lotsBefore, lotsAfter, handDatedLotsReplaced, syncLotsReplaced, realisedPnl, adjustedFor, q, net, openingQty {before, after}, openCostAfter, brokerCost, costDelta, costNote, digest), notHeld and unmatched {securities, trades} and the overall digest. 400 portfolio.wrong_file_kind (extension detected: dividends for a dividend payout list - import it as dividends -, tradebook_without_sides for a tradebook with no buy/sell column); 400 portfolio.invalid (field file: unreadable, too big, missing columns - with the accepted names -, not UTF-8; accountId); 404 portfolio.not_found (account); 409 portfolio.role_off

Import a tradebook: body multipart/form-data with accountId, file, rebuild (true | false, default true) and digest (required with rebuild: the digest of the preview). Stores the trades the account does not have yet as one batch (a trade id of the file together with the trade date - exchanges number trades per day -, else a hash of the line, is the identity: the same file again stores nothing and makes no batch) and, with rebuild, replaces the lots of every holding whose result is ok by lots built from the real buy and sell dates. Trades of securities not held, of mismatching or ambiguous holdings are stored and not applied. 409 portfolio.preview_stale when holdings, lots, corporate actions or trades changed since the preview (extension report: the fresh preview; nothing applied); 409 portfolio.sync_running while a holdings sync or a trades run of the account runs (a ledger-only run does not block it); 400 portfolio.wrong_file_kind (extension detected: dividends | tradebook_without_sides, as for the preview); 400 portfolio.invalid; 404 portfolio.not_found. Audited with counts only

Add one trade by hand: holdingId, or accountId with symbol and/or isin of an NSE share or ETF of the instrument master; side buy | sell, tradeDate (1990-01-02 to today), tradeTime (optional, India time), quantity (whole, above 0), price (above 0), charges (optional). Validated like a CSV row; identical manual trades are not deduplicated. Changes no lots - rebuild them afterwards. 400 portfolio.invalid with field errors; 404 portfolio.not_found. Audited
Void a trade: it stops counting, is never deleted and can be imported again. Voiding a voided trade is a no-op. Changes no lots - rebuild them afterwards. 404 portfolio.not_found. Audited

get.summary: The imports of tradebook files, newest first: accountId (optional), page, pageSize (max 100, default 50). Each has id, accountId, accountName, fileName, sha256, parsed, imported, duplicates, skipped, bad, status imported | undone, activeTrades, securities, createdBy, createdAt, undoneAt

post.summary: Undo an import: voids its trades (nothing is deleted) and rebuilds from the remaining trades the lots of the affected holdings whose lots came from trades - with none left, one lot of the broker's quantity and cost dated by the first import date, flagged default. LIMITATION: an undo cannot bring back lots the owner dated by hand or a sync added that an earlier rebuild replaced; handDatedLotsReplaced and syncLotsReplaced say how many the rebuild removes (the lots of holdings it rebuilds). Holdings whose lots did not come from trades keep their lots; holdings that cannot be rebuilt (quantity mismatch, ambiguous) keep theirs and are listed in notRebuilt [{symbol, holdingId, reason}] (holdingsNotRebuilt counts them). dryRun=true (default false) changes nothing and returns the same result (dryRun, applied=false) so the confirmation can say what will happen. Undoing twice is a no-op (alreadyUndone). 409 portfolio.sync_running while a holdings sync or a trades run of the account runs, with a message that it can take a few minutes (a ledger-only run does not block it; a dry run and an already undone batch never wait); 404 portfolio.not_found. Audited with counts only

get.summary: The trades of a holding's security (by ISIN, else symbol), newest first, voided ones included and flagged (voided, voidedAt, voidedBy): page, pageSize (max 200, default 50)

post.summary: Rebuild a holding's lots from its stored trades. dryRun (default true) returns the rebuild block - status, counts of lots replaced, realised profit, adjustments, the broker's quantity against the trades - and changes nothing; dryRun=false replaces the lots when the status is ok (applied) and leaves them for unchanged, quantity_mismatch and ambiguous. A holding without trades is rebuilt into one default-dated lot. 409 portfolio.sync_running while a holdings sync or a trades run of the account runs, with a message that it can take a few minutes (a ledger-only run does not block it; a dry run never waits); 404 portfolio.not_found. Audited with counts only

Sync now: read the account's trades and then its ledger from Dhan (needs the Portfolio role and a connected Dhan token). Optional body {from} (an India date from 1990-01-02 to today): the first date to read instead of the watermark - for an account never read, its first import date. An earlier date than the watermark reads dates again (nothing is stored twice); a date later than the day after the watermark of either kind is refused, because the dates in between would never be read (when only one kind was read so far, also a date later than the account's first import date, because the other kind would then begin at the chosen date). The dates are read in windows of at most 30 days; new trades are stored next to the imported ones (source broker) and the lots of the holdings are rebuilt from the real dates where that is safe. Answers at once with the trades run as it begins (status running); poll the status. 409 portfolio.sync_running while a holdings sync or another trades or ledger run of the account runs; 409 portfolio.not_connected or portfolio.token_expired without a usable Dhan token; 400 portfolio.invalid (field from: not a plausible date, or leaves a hole after the watermark); 404 accounts.not_found. Audited with counts only

get.summary: The status of the trades and ledger sync: running, for each kind the watermark (last date read), the latest run (status, dates, counts, error) and windowsDone / windowsTotal, the next scheduled run (null when the service is paused) and, from the latest SUCCEEDED trades run and no other (nothing is carried forward from older runs; a skipped, failed or running run neither changes nor erases them): holdingsRebuilt, holdingsNeedingReview (a hand-dated lot; use the holding's rebuild preview) and needsReviewSymbols (their trading symbols, at most 50; holdingsNeedingReview says how many in all). Health (ADR 0027): each kind also has attempts (the number of the latest run within the day's occurrence: 1 for the first, up to 4 with the three quiet retries), consecutiveFailedDays (days in a row whose last attempt failed; 0 when the latest succeeded), lastFailureReason (unavailable, rate_limited, interrupted, rejected, history_too_large, token_expired, token_refused, not_connected, data_changed, unexpected; null while healthy) and retryAt (when the next quiet retry is due, null when none is pending); the run counts carry attempts, failureReason and deepenedTo. deepenedTo is the earliest date the nightly deepening of the trade history reached (one earlier year a night while the trades do not explain a holding in a way earlier history could fix; null: none read) and deepenExhausted that it reads no more (Dhan's history ends there or the furthest year back is reached). Dropped rows (roadmap ISS-03): each kind also has droppedByReason (how many rows the latest run of that kind dropped per reason code; a later clean or skipped run shows none: unreadable_row, missing_id, bad_id, missing_side, bad_quantity, bad_price, bad_time for trades; bad_date, missing_amount, bad_amount, zero_amount for the ledger; failed_checks, store_refused, other) and droppedRows (from the same latest run: the place of the first five: windowFrom, windowTo, page, rowIndex, reason - never a row's content); the same two fields are in the run counts (lastRun.counts), where droppedByReason adds up to dropped. Old runs have both empty

The account's ledger entries read from Dhan, newest first: from, to (India dates, inclusive), class (funds_in, funds_out, dividend, charges, other), page, pageSize (max 200, default 50). Each entry has date, voucherNo, description, narration (Dhan's free text - show as plain text), exchange, amount (signed: credit minus debit), class and runningBalance. totals lists the count and signed amount of every class for the period from to to, whatever class is filtered. The ledger's entries of class charges count as costs in the net returns of an account and the portfolio, and an entry of class dividend is offered as a suggested dividend (see the dividends endpoints); nothing else of the ledger is part of returns

post.summary: Add a dividend you received: holdingId (the account is then the holding's) or accountId alone (unallocated: no holding); payDate (1990-01-02 to today, India), amount (rupees, above 0), perShare (optional, above 0), note (optional plain text, at most 200 characters). The same account, holding, date and amount as a dividend that is not voided is a possible duplicate: 409 portfolio.possible_duplicate, repeat with confirm true to add the second payment. 400 portfolio.invalid with field errors; 404 portfolio.not_found (account); 409 portfolio.role_off. Audited with the id only, never the amount
Void a dividend: it stops counting in the figures and is never deleted. Voiding a voided dividend is a no-op. 404 portfolio.not_found. Audited with the id only

get.summary: The dividends entered for a holding, newest first (pay date), voided ones included and flagged (voided, voidedAt, voidedBy): page, pageSize (max 200, default 50)
The dividends entered for an account - every holding's and the unallocated ones (holdingId null) - newest first, voided ones included and flagged: page, pageSize (max 200, default 50)

The suggested dividends of an account: its ledger entries of class dividend that were not accepted or dismissed yet, newest first (the ledger entry shape: id, date, amount, description and narration - Dhan's free text, show as plain text): page, pageSize (max 200, default 50). Dhan's documented ledger has no entry for an ordinary dividend, so this is usually empty. Nothing is added without accepting

post.summary: Accept a suggested dividend: creates a dividend of the ledger entry's amount and date, for the holding you choose in the optional body {holdingId, note} (one of the account's) or unallocated, and remembers the decision (final; voiding the dividend later does not bring the suggestion back). 404 portfolio.not_found (not a dividend entry of the account); 409 portfolio.conflict (decided meanwhile), portfolio.role_off. Audited with ids only

Dismiss a suggested dividend: it is not offered again; nothing else changes. The decision is final. 404 portfolio.not_found (not a dividend entry of the account); 409 portfolio.conflict (decided meanwhile). Audited with ids only

Read a dividend payout file against an account and say what importing it would do, storing and changing nothing. Body: multipart/form-data with accountId (an account with the Portfolio role) and file (CSV, UTF-8, at most 10 MB and 20,000 data rows; header: a date, a scrip name or symbol or ISIN, and the amount paid (Dividend Paid, Dividend Amount, Payout; a plain Amount or Net Amount only beside a Dividend Per Share or DPS column) - for example Date, Scrip Name, Dividend Per Share, Quantity, Dividend Paid - names accepted in any case with punctuation ignored; dates like 13 Jun 2024, 23 Sept 2024, 2024-06-13, 13-06-2024; amounts like 1,134.00). Returns format dividends, the file (rows, parsed, parsedAmount, repeated and identicalRepeats - rows identical to an earlier row are counted once -, distinct, bad rows with line and reason - at most 200 listed, badTotal counts all -, alreadyImported, possibleDuplicates, toAdd, needsMatch, ambiguous), the items (line, payDate, name, nameKey - the name as the server compares names: two spellings of one company have one nameKey, so group rows and key choices by it -, perShare, quantity, amount, status new | imported | possible_duplicate | needs_match | ambiguous, match {kind alias | isin | symbol | name | contains | master | choice | none, holdingId, instrumentId, symbol, isin, name, candidates}, warnings amount_mismatch | before_first_lot | partial_name_match), totals {count, amount, byYear} of what would be added, beforeFirstLot {count, amount, firstLotDate} and the digest. 400 portfolio.wrong_file_kind (extension detected: trades | tradebook_without_sides for a tradebook, statement for a file of a date, a name and a plain Amount with nothing in the header that says dividend - the kind is judged from the header before any column is read); 400 portfolio.invalid (field file: unreadable, too big, missing columns - with the accepted names -, not UTF-8; accountId); 404 portfolio.not_found (account); 409 portfolio.role_off

Import a dividend payout file: body multipart/form-data with accountId, file, digest (required: the digest of the preview), choices (optional JSON array of {name, holdingId | instrumentId | none, remember}: what a scrip name of the file means - name is the name as written or the item's nameKey; choices for spellings with one nameKey that agree are one choice, ones that disagree are a 400; remember saves it as an alias for later files) and includeDuplicates (optional JSON array of the lines of possible duplicates to import anyway). Stores the rows that are to be added as one batch of dividends with source csv, each with an identity (account, date, normalised name, per share, quantity, amount - the same file again stores nothing and makes no batch; rows identical within a file count once), the file's quantity and, when no holding is matched, the file's scrip name (unallocated; nothing is guessed). Answers imported, amount, allocated, instrumentOnly, unallocated, alreadyImported, possibleDuplicatesSkipped, aliasesSaved and the batch (preview again for the report). 409 portfolio.preview_stale when holdings, remembered names or dividends changed since the preview (extension report: the fresh preview; nothing stored); 400 portfolio.invalid (digest; choices naming no row of the file or no holding of the account, or contradicting each other for one nameKey; form fields too long or too many); 400 portfolio.wrong_file_kind (as for the preview); 404 portfolio.not_found. Audited with counts and ids only

get.summary: The imports of dividend files, newest first: accountId (optional), page, pageSize (max 100, default 50). Each has id, accountId, accountName, fileName, sha256, parsed, imported, duplicates, bad, amount, status imported | undone, activeDividends, createdBy, createdAt, undoneAt

post.summary: Undo an import: voids its dividends (nothing is deleted; they stop counting in every figure) and marks the batch undone; the same file can be imported again afterwards. Remembered names stay. Undoing twice is a no-op (alreadyUndone, voided 0). 404 portfolio.not_found. Audited with counts and the batch id only

Recognise downloaded files by their title and header and say what importing each would do, storing and changing nothing. Body: multipart/form-data with accountId (an account with the Portfolio role), files (one or more, at most 20, 10 MB each; CSV, XLS or XLSX - the format is judged from the first bytes) and optionally choices (a JSON array of {name, holdingId | instrumentId | isin, remember}: what scrip names of a global transaction report mean; name is the name as written or the item's nameKey, and the choice applies to every file). Answers one result per file, in order: fileName, kind (global_transaction_report | dp_charges | demat_holding | pnl_report | trades | dividends | tradebook_without_sides | statement | unknown), supported, routeTo (dividends: import it on the dividend import), message (why a file cannot be imported), error (code and message: unreadable file, or portfolio.wrong_file_kind for an unknown shape - the message lists the accepted kinds), summary {rows, valid, toAdd, alreadyImported, skipped, bad, from, to}, warnings [{code, message, count}] (other_account, bad_rows, needs_match, partial_name_match, charges_differ_from_footer, negative_charges, value_not_reproduced, covered_by_dhan, totals_differ, holdings_differ, notice_only), and the block of the kind: trades (the tradebook preview of ADR 0023, as for a global transaction report: lots, hand-dated lots replaced, realised profit, digest) with bill {names [{name, nameKey, symbolHint, status resolved | ambiguous | needs_match, kind, isin, symbol, holdingId, instrumentId, rows, trades, candidates}], needsMatch, coverage {covered, differences}, charges {total, reportTotal, matches}} for a global transaction report, costs {lines, counts, amountToStore, names} for depository charges, demat {asOf, securities, matching, quantityDifferences, heldNotSynced, syncedNotInStatement, names} for a demat statement - which changes no holding and raises no notice. digest fingerprints what is shown. The personal lines of a report (name, client code, mobile, e-mail) are never read into the answer. 400 portfolio.invalid (form fields); 404 portfolio.not_found (account); 409 portfolio.role_off

Import downloaded files: body multipart/form-data with accountId, files (as for the preview), digests (a JSON array with the preview's digest, or null, for each file in order; required for depository charges and demat statements, and for trade files with rebuild), choices (as for the preview; remember saves a choice for later files), rebuild (true | false, default true: rebuild the lots of the holdings whose result is ok, like a tradebook import) and acceptOtherAccount (a JSON array of the indexes, from 0, of files to import although the report's client code (UCC) differs from that of the reports imported into the account before; the first import with a code remembers its hash - never the code - and an account that remembers none never warns). Each file is imported on its own, all or nothing, and answers: fileName, kind, status (imported | nothing_new | not_supported | rejected), message, error, preview (the fresh preview when the confirmed one went stale: error portfolio.preview_stale, nothing stored), trades (a TradeImportResult: batch, imported, alreadyImported, rebuilt, holdingsRebuilt, lotsReplaced, report - undo it with the trade batch endpoint), costs (batch, imported, amount, alreadyImported, alreadyInLedger, namesLearned - undo it with the cost batch endpoint), demat (namesLearned, namesKnown) and aliasesSaved. A global transaction report is stored as bill-level trades; a trade the broker's own history has for the same day, ISIN and side is left out, and bill-level rows are voided as superseded when the broker sync later stores such trades. 400 portfolio.invalid; 404 portfolio.not_found; 409 portfolio.role_off; 409 portfolio.sync_running (a file waits for the runs it would race, and the message says it can take a few minutes: a trade file - a tradebook or a Dhan report's bills - while a holdings sync or a trades run of the account runs; a depository-charges sheet while a holdings sync or a ledger run runs; a demat statement never waits; the preview never waits). Audited with counts only

get.summary: The imports of depository-charges sheets, newest first: accountId (optional), page, pageSize (max 100, default 50). Each has id, accountId, accountName, fileName, sha256, parsed, imported, duplicates, bad, amount, status imported | undone, activeEntries, createdBy, createdAt, undoneAt

post.summary: Undo a depository-charges import: voids its cost entries (nothing is deleted; they stop counting in the net figures) and marks the batch undone; the same sheet can be imported again afterwards. Learned names stay. Undoing twice is a no-op (alreadyUndone, voided 0). 404 portfolio.not_found. Audited with counts and the batch id only

get.summary: State of the live price feed from its heartbeat (same fields as the hub event feedStatus): state (connected, idle, connecting, reconnecting, closed, paused, no_token, token_refused, flapping, or not_running when it has not reported for 60 seconds), subscribed instruments and the exchange time of its latest tick

post.summary: Read and compile a strategy text (413 over 256 KB); the answer is valid (no error), the hash and the located problems. An invalid text is still 200. Writes nothing

get.summary: The JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) of the strategy file, for the editor
The strategy families with their latest version number, the number of versions and whether they are built in

post.summary: Store a valid text (413 over 256 KB) as a new family (201) or as the next version of one (201); the same content again is the same version (200, nothing written). 422 lab.invalid_strategy with the problems; 409 lab.version_exists when the text's version is not the next number, lab.builtin_readonly for a built-in

get.summary: One strategy family with the list of its versions
One stored version: the text as posted, hash, parent hash, note and whether the text is free of errors under today's rules
The text of a stored version as a YAML file (attachment); posted to validate it gives the same hash

post.summary: The text of a stored version with a new id (a built-in gets <ID>_COPY) and the parent hash to post with it; stores nothing

Queue a quick test of a stored strategy version on a basket or a list of symbols (202 with the run); the same input again returns the run that holds it (200). 422 lab.invalid_input, 404 lab.not_found, 409 lab.no_data

get.summary: Lab runs, newest first; filter by strategyId and state; limit 1 to 200 (default 50)
One Lab run: state, stage, progress, the simulation run keys, counts, located problems, the stage log and the labels (cost basis, sample, exploration)

The report of a succeeded full or robust run, built from the stored result: verdict, gates, figures, best cells, warnings, honest limits, a deterministic plain-English summary. 409 lab.no_report for any other run
The report as one static, inert HTML page
The report as a zip folder (report.json, report.html, summary.txt, README.txt, manifest.json), identical bytes for the same report

post.summary: Stop a run: a queued run at once, a running run at its next safe point between instruments (202); nothing is stored for it. 409 lab.not_cancellable once it has finished

get.summary: The test ledger of a strategy family: every Lab run created for it, the number of distinct variants (hashes) and the factor the qualification gates are tightened by now

What the learning engine holds: rows in the newest cell snapshot and its date; and for models, experiments, hypotheses, lessons and the changelog the count of the newest 200 (flagged when there may be more), the split by role, outcome or state, and the newest record with its stored verdict. Nothing is computed or scored; the limits (about 2.1 years, few folds, modelled fills) are listed. Empty before the first record.

The cell statistics of the newest snapshot: per cell and window (all, 250d, 60d) the trades, the Beta-shrunk win rate with its credible bounds, recency-weighted expectancy and profit factor, drawdown and MAE/MFE quantiles, each with its basis, knobs and limits. Filter by strategy and window; empty before the first computation. 422 learning.invalid
One cell (key strategy|tf|side|style|exit|regime, URL-encoded) in its windows from the newest snapshot that holds it. 404 learning.cell_not_found

The registered models, newest first (limit 1 to 200, default 50; role challenger, champion or retired filters on the current role): hash, the training set, the validation verdict against the baselines (Eligible, CannotBeatBaselines or Inconclusive) with its reasons and pooled numbers, and the role. Advisory: nothing uses a model until P7. Empty before the first registration. 422 learning.invalid

One model with its parameters, the full validation report with its honest limits, the calibration table, the feature importance (path-based, not exact, not SHAP) and every designation. No model bytes. 404 models.not_found

The recorded experiments (knob changes judged against a baseline run), newest first (limit 1 to 200, default 50): the knob, the outcome (Better, NotBetter, Inconclusive or CheaperAssumption), folds better of folds used, the improvement required after the trials, totals after the expected live gap, and the measured time of the comparison. Empty before the first experiment. 422 learning.invalid
One experiment with its full report, honest limits and the rules it was judged with. 404 experiments.not_found

The learning changelog, newest first (limit 1 to 200, default 50; subjectKind cell or model; subject one cell key or model:ID): what changed, by whom or what, why, before and after references and evidence ids. Rows are never changed; a revert is a row that points at the one it reverts. Empty before the first record. 422 learning.invalid

Where a cell is (query cell=strategy|tf|side|style|exit|regime), replayed from its changelog rows, with the moves the lifecycle allows next. A record only: nothing acts on a cell's state before paper data and live exist. 422 learning.invalid
One changelog row. 404 changelog.not_found

The hypotheses (one knob each, from the owner or the grid), newest first, each in its current state (proposed, approved, running, judged, accepted, rejected, expired); optional state filter, limit 1 to 200 (default 50). Empty before the first. 422 learning.invalid
One hypothesis with its history, the states it may move to and the experiment that judged it. Accepting records a verdict only; applying a change is the owner's own act. 404 hypotheses.not_found

The lessons (a problem a replayed monitor found, the fix linked and the stored result), newest first, each in its current state (open, linked, closed, dismissed); optional state filter, limit 1 to 200 (default 50). Empty before the first. 422 learning.invalid
One lesson with its history, the states it may move to and the before and after numbers of its closing. Linking or closing applies nothing. 404 lessons.not_found

The plans, newest session first, each in its current state; optional session date and account filters, limit 1 to 200 (default 50). Empty before the first. No order is placed by any plan. 422 plans.invalid

One plan with its tickets (primary, reserve, rejected with reasons and evidence), size per account, the states they may move to and the trail of every state change. Armed means watched, never an order. 404 plans.not_found

The grade of every ticket of a plan (primary, reserve, rejected), each walked through the stored bars of its session and labelled 'simulated on plan prices', with the day's top-1/3/5/all curves and decision groups. A ticket without a stored grade is pending. Read only. 404 plans.not_found

Top-1/3/5/all curves by rank, primary versus reserve versus rejected, and the owner's decisions (approved, modified, rejected, lapsed, undecided) over the graded plans of an optional date range, with sample-size notes. Labelled 'simulated on plan prices'. Read only. 422 plans.invalid

The recorded attempts of the nightly pipeline, newest planned session first: published (with the plan) or failed closed (with the gate and the reason). Optional planned-session date, limit 1 to 200 (default 50). Read only. 422 plans.invalid
The autonomy settings in force (automatic approval and reserve promotion, both OFF = manual approval by default) with the history of changes. No order is placed in any setting

put.summary: Change the autonomy settings as the owner; appends an audited row. Needs a session, the CSRF token and the password in the body, checked on EVERY change (an earlier step-up window does not count and is not used up). 401 auth.invalid_credentials, 423 auth.locked, 403 autonomy.owner_only, 400 autonomy.values_invalid or autonomy.reason_invalid, 409 autonomy.stale

AcceptSuggestionInput.description: Accepting a suggested dividend: optionally the holding it is for (one of the account's; none: unallocated) and a note. The amount and the date are the ledger entry's.

AccountDetail.description:
Everything about one account. Secret values and tokens are never part of it (only set / not set); the client id is masked. ApiKeyIssuedOn and
ApiKeyExpiresOn are the day the Dhan API key was generated and the first day it is no longer valid (12 months). TokenStatus repeats Connection.Status.

AccountEventView.description: One audit entry of an account.

AccountOverrides.description: Per-account replacements for values of the risk profile; null means "use the profile's value".

AccountResponse.description: What the owner may see about their own account (never the hash or the lockout state).

AccountSummary.description:
One row of the accounts list. Broker is "dhan"; MaskedClientId shows the first four and last two characters; Secrets lists the
secret fields with set / not set; ApiKeyExpiresOn is the first day the Dhan API key is no longer valid; TokenStatus repeats
Connection.Status (for the list's health dot).

ActionCounts.description: What the Action center counts for the scope (before the status filter): items by state, and for the open items by rule (all seven rules, zeros included) and by severity (high, medium, info). `NoPrice` counts open holdings without a usable price (no price-based rule can fire for them).

ActionDecisionView.description: The outcome of a decision: `State``open|snoozed|done`, `SnoozedUntil`, and the item as it is now (null when the id is not produced by a rule now, which only a reopen can still ask about).

ActionItem.description:
One Action-center item. `Id` is stable (`{rule}:{holdingId}`, or `sector_concentration:{accountId}:{12 hex}`) and safe in a URL path. `Rule` is one of `below_cost`, `large_gain`, `overweight`, `sector_concentration`,
`long_term_soon`, `lagging_nifty`, `not_in_basket`; `Severity``high|medium|info`; `HoldingId`, `InstrumentId` and `Symbol` are null for an account-level item (concentration) and `InstrumentId` for a holding that is not in the
master list. `Title` and `Detail` are plain sentences; `Numbers` the figures behind them; `Suggestions` the buttons that make sense (`open|set_alert|add_to_basket|snooze|done`). `State` is `open|snoozed|done`;
`SnoozedUntil` the India date a snoozed item shows again. Severity, text and numbers are recomputed on every read.

ActionList.description: The items of the status asked for, most important first, and the counts of the whole scope.

ActionNumbers.description: The figures that made an item fire; which ones are set depends on the rule, the others are null. below_cost, large_gain: `PnlPct`, `Pnl`, `Invested`, `Value`, `ThresholdPct` (the band reached: 10 or 20 / 25). overweight: `WeightPct` of the account's priced value, `ThresholdPct` (the limit), `Positions` (priced positions of the account), `Value`. sector_concentration: `Sector`, `SectorSharePct` of the account's priced value, `ThresholdPct`, `SectorValue`, `Positions` (in the sector), `LargestSymbol`, `LargestHoldingId` and `LargestValue` of the largest holding in it. long_term_soon: `Lots`, `PnlPct`. lagging_nifty: `HeldDays`, `XirrPct`, `BenchmarkXirrPct`, `GapPp` (holding minus benchmark, negative), `ThresholdPp`. not_in_basket: `Invested`, `Value` (null when unpriced).

ActionThresholds.description: The thresholds of the Action-center rules (ADR 0022, doc 15 §3): percentages are percent numbers (10 = 10 %). The defaults are the ones of the design; the owner edits them in Settings within the fixed ranges below.

ActionThresholdsInput.description: The thresholds to save: every value is required. `MinPositions`, `LagDays` and `LongTermWindowDays` must be whole numbers.

ActionThresholdsView.description: The thresholds in force with the documented defaults; `IsDefault` when they are the defaults; `UpdatedBy`/`UpdatedAt` null while none are stored.

ActionUnavailable.description: Rules that could not be evaluated: `Lagging` holdings held long enough for the lagging-Nifty rule but without a usable benchmark or XIRR.

AddCorporateActionRequest.description:
A corporate action to add by hand (it is applied at once). `exDate``yyyy-MM-dd` (2000-01-01 to a year ahead); `kind` split|bonus; `numerator` and `denominator` whole numbers 1 to 100000
(a split 1:1 changes nothing and is refused); `note` at most 200 characters. `acknowledgeCsvAdjusted` true says the owner knows the loaded CSV files are adjusted up to `csvAdjustedThrough`
and wants an ex-date on or before it anyway (otherwise 409 `data.csv_already_adjusted`).

AddMembersInput.description: Instruments to add (1 to 500; repeats count once) with an optional note stored on each new membership.

AddMembersResult.description:
What an add did (counts of distinct instruments): `added` became members, `alreadyMembers` were members already, `newlyTracked` of the added
ones were not tracked and are now. `memberCount` = members now.

AdjustmentActionView.description: One applied action in the `adjustment` block of a bars read: the ex-date, kind, ratio and the factor of the action itself.

AdjustmentView.description:
What an adjusted read applied: `applied` is the number of applied actions that changed the bars returned (those with an ex-date after the oldest bar), `factor` the cumulative factor of the oldest bar
returned (the strongest; newer bars have a factor closer to 1) and `actions` those actions, oldest ex-date first.

AggregatePhase.description:
The aggregate phase of a data job (ADR 0016 §6): `Done` of `Total` are instruments. `Buckets` counts the bars written (new or changed),
by timeframe; `Full` is true when everything was rebuilt rather than the ranges touched by this job. Part of the API (the job's `aggregate` block).

AggregatesCheck.description: Aggregates against the 1-minute bars: every stored 5m, 10m, 15m, 30m, 1h, 1D, 1W and 1M bucket in the window recomputed independently and compared exactly (OHLC, volume, bar count).

AggregatesOverview.description: The derived timeframes: per timeframe, when they were last built and how many instruments have changes that are not aggregated yet.

AttentionAction.description:
What the owner can do about an item (ADR 0027), at most two per item. `Kind``route`: `Target` is an in-app path with its query (`/accounts?account=…&tab=connection`) to navigate to. `Kind``command`: `Target` is an existing
endpoint as `METHOD /api/path` (`POST /api/accounts/{id}/sync/broker-history`), which the browser calls with its session and CSRF token like any other call of the app - no new surface.

AutoRefreshView.description: The daily automatic refresh: whether it is on, at what India time, and when it runs next.

id.description: The row in force; null while nothing was ever stored (defaults, all OFF).

notice.description: No order is placed in any setting.

AutonomySettingsView.description: The settings in force, with the history newest first.

BadBar.description: A bar that broke a row rule: its start and what is wrong with it.

BarRow.description: One bar. Times of the day timeframes (`1D 1W 1M`) are India midnight of the first day of the bucket. `bars` counts the 1-minute bars in it; `complete` says none was missing. `source` (1m only): csv · dhan.

BarsOverview.description:
The stored 1-minute bars: instruments with bars, the first bar and the last bar (the "last tick"), how many trading days (by the trading calendar: weekdays without the holidays, with the special sessions) the last bar is behind the last
closed session (`expectedSession`: 15:30 India time, or the end of a special session, has passed), `stale` (behind) and how many instruments are behind or still empty (tracked without bars).

BasketHistory.description: The newest additions and removals of a basket, newest first.

BasketHistoryEntry.description: An addition (`kind` = added, `by` = who added it) or removal (`kind` = removed, `by` = who removed it) of an instrument. Only additions carry a note (the one given when adding); a removal has none.

BasketInput.description: Attributes of a basket (create and replace). Missing colour = the default; missing purpose = trading; blank description = none.

BasketMemberView.description:
One stay of an instrument in a basket: `validFrom` = when it was added, `validTo` = when it was removed (null while it is a member),
`position` = place among the members (0 first), `addedBy` = the owner's address.
In a system (portfolio) basket a member is the instrument of the bucket's holdings: `id` = the (first) holding, `validFrom` = when the holding was first seen,
`addedBy` = "portfolio", `quantity` = units held (summed over the bucket's holdings of it) and `accountName` = the account(s) holding it; both are null in a manual basket.

BasketMembers.description:
The members of a basket, in their order. `asOf` is null for the current members, otherwise the India date they are as of (members at the end of that
day; removed ones show their `validTo`). `total` counts the items.

BasketOrderInput.description: Every active basket exactly once, in the wanted order.

BasketView.description:
A basket. `purpose`: trading · long_term · watch. `position` = place among the active baskets (0 first; the system baskets count on their own, in their group).
`memberCount` = instruments in it now. `archivedAt` is null for an active basket (archived ones are only listed on request).
`kind`: manual (the owner's) · portfolio (an account's portfolio bucket, ADR 0014); `system` = true for the latter: read-only, never archived, its members are the
bucket's current holdings. `accountId`/`accountName` are set for the default bucket of an account.

BenchmarkInput.description: Sets the benchmark: the id of a master-list index.

BenchmarkView.description: The benchmark in force (all null when the master list has no such index yet). `IsDefault`: the owner has not chosen one, Nifty 50 applies.

BillCandidate.description: A security a name may mean: `Isin`, `Symbol`, `Name` and — when it is a holding of the account or a share of the instrument master — `HoldingId` or `InstrumentId`.

BillCharges.description: The charges of the report's rows added up (`Total`, every row, whatever becomes of it) against the report's own total charges (`ReportTotal`; null when the report has none); `Matches` within ₹0.01.

BillCoverage.description: What the broker's own trades cover (ADR 0029): `Covered` trades of the report are left out because Dhan's trade history has the same day, ISIN and side; the days whose totals differ are listed (at most 50; `DifferencesTotal` counts all).

BillDetails.description: What is particular to a global transaction report: the names (every one that is a share or ETF, at most 500 listed; `NamesTotal` counts all) with what they mean, how many are unresolved, the coverage by the broker's trades and the charges check.

BillDifference.description: A day, security and side whose total quantity differs between the report's bill rows and the broker's own trades (the broker's win; shown, not hidden).

BillNameView.description:
A scrip name of a global transaction report. `Name` is the name as written (plain text, untrusted), `NameKey` the name reduced to what the server compares names by (key the choices by it), `SymbolHint` the ticker in brackets. `Status`: `resolved`,
`ambiguous` (more than one security fits: `Candidates`) or `needs_match` (none: its trades are kept without an ISIN). `Kind` is the rule that decided: `choice`, `alias`, `symbol`, `holding`, `master`, `learned` (a demat or depository file taught
it), `partial` (a spelling that differs by a word's ending: check it), `none`.

BrokerDroppedRow.description: Where one dropped row of a broker read lies, and why it was dropped: the dates of the request that returned it (DateOnly BrokerDroppedRow.WindowFrom, DateOnly BrokerDroppedRow.WindowTo; after a split, the half that was asked), the int BrokerDroppedRow.Page of the answer (0 for the ledger, which has one) and the zero-based int BrokerDroppedRow.RowIndex of the row in that answer, so the owner can look the row up in Dhan's own statement. Location and reason code only: never a name, symbol, amount, id or narration of the row (roadmap ISS-03).

BrokerHistoryInput.description: Optional body of "Sync now" for the broker history: the first date to read, instead of the watermark (or, for an account never read, the first import date).

BrokerHistoryRunView.description: The answer of "Sync now": the trades run and, when it succeeded and has been carried on to it, the ledger run. Started over the API, the answer holds the trades run as it begins (`running`); the status says how far both are.

BrokerHistoryStatusView.description: The status of the broker history sync of an account: whether a run is running, both kinds, the next scheduled run (null when the service is paused or there is none) and three figures that come from the latest succeeded trades run and from no other (nothing is carried forward from older runs, and a run that was skipped, failed or is still running does not change them): `HoldingsRebuilt` (rebuilt automatically by that run), `HoldingsNeedingReview` (a hand-dated lot; the owner uses the holding's rebuild preview) and `NeedsReviewSymbols`, the trading symbols of those holdings (at most 50, in the order the run listed them: alphabetical; `HoldingsNeedingReview` says how many there are in all). A quiet run that skipped the rebuild because nothing changed reports 0 rebuilt (holdings that need review are never skipped: every run looks at them again). `DeepenedTo` is the earliest date the nightly deepening of the trade history reached (null: it has not read an earlier year) and `DeepenExhausted` that it reads no more years (Dhan's history ends there, or the furthest year back is reached; ADR 0027).

BrokerIdView.description: The id a broker uses for the instrument (Dhan: security id + exchange segment).

droppedByReason.description: Why the latest run of this kind dropped rows (roadmap ISS-03): the number per reason code, the same figures as `LastRun.Counts.DroppedByReason`. Only the latest run counts: a later clean or skipped run shows none (empty when that run dropped none, or when there is no run, or it ran before the reasons were recorded). The codes are listed on `BrokerDropReasons`.

droppedRows.description: The place of the first five rows the latest run of this kind dropped (dates of the request, page, row index, reason code) - never the rows' content; a later clean or skipped run shows none. The same as `LastRun.Counts.DroppedRows`.

BrokerKindStatus.description:
How far one kind is read: the `Watermark` (last date read; null when nothing was read yet), the latest run and its windows done of total. The health (ADR 0027): `Attempts` is the number of the latest run within the day's occurrence (1 for the first, up to 4 with
the three quiet retries; 0 while there is no run), `ConsecutiveFailedDays` the days in a row whose last attempt failed (0 when the latest attempt succeeded), `LastFailureReason` a code (`unavailable`, `rate_limited`, `interrupted`, `rejected`,
`history_too_large`, `token_expired`, `token_refused`, `not_connected`, `data_changed`, `unexpected`; null while healthy) and `RetryAt` when the next quiet retry is due (null when none is pending). While a retry is pending the owner is told nothing. `DroppedByReason` and `DroppedRows` say why the latest run dropped rows (see below).

BrokerNotRebuilt.description:
A holding (or security) the automatic rebuild after a trade sync left alone, and why: `needs_review`, `quantity_mismatch`, `ambiguous`, `no_holding` or `changed_meanwhile`. The symbol is a ticker, never trade content.
`Detail` is the kind of mismatch for `quantity_mismatch` (`negative_opening`, `sell_exceeds_open`, `fractional_after_adjustment`: the first two are what an earlier read of the history can fix) and
`HoldingId` the single holding it is about (null for a security without one), so that a notice can open it.

droppedByReason.description: Why rows were dropped: the number of int BrokerSyncCounts.Dropped rows per reason code (`missing_id`, `bad_quantity`, `zero_amount` ...; see `BrokerDropReasons`). Empty in a run recorded before ISS-03 and when nothing was dropped; the figures add up to int BrokerSyncCounts.Dropped for a run that has them.

droppedRows.description: The location of the first int BrokerDrops.MaxLocations dropped rows of the run (request dates, page, row index and reason code) - never their content.

enriched.description: Trades stored already (counted in int BrokerSyncCounts.Duplicates too) that got an ISIN, charges or ticker they lacked from this read.

emptyByNoData.description: Windows (or half-windows) taken as empty only because Dhan answered DH-907 to the first page.

attempts.description: The number of this attempt within the occurrence: 1 for the first, up to 4 with the three retries. 0 for a run recorded before ADR 0027 (read as 1).

failureReason.description: The plain reason code of why the run failed; null while it runs and when it succeeded.

deepenedTo.description: The earliest date a read of earlier history reached in this run (null: none was made).

superseded.description: Trades run: bill-level rows of an imported Dhan report that the trades of this run replaced. Ledger run: imported depository-charge entries that the charges of this run replaced. Voided as superseded, ADR 0029.

supersededDiffering.description: Of the replaced rows' day-security-side groups, how many had a different total quantity than the broker's trades.

rereadVersion.description: The version of the Dhan mapping the windows in IReadOnlyList<BrokerWindowSpan> BrokerSyncCounts.RereadDone were read again with (0: none were read again). A failed run's list is only taken over by the run that follows it when the version is still the same (ADR 0030).

rereadDone.description:
The windows read again since the mapping changed (ADR 0027) that are done: each is added in the unit of work that stores the window, so a run that fails later does not make the retry read them again (ADR 0030). The run that follows a failed
one starts with the failed run's list (same int BrokerSyncCounts.RereadVersion) and adds its own. Dates only.

BrokerSyncCounts.description:
What a broker history run did (ADR 0025), kept as JSON on the run. int BrokerSyncCounts.WindowsDone of int BrokerSyncCounts.WindowsTotal date windows are read and stored; int BrokerSyncCounts.Halved windows were split in half because Dhan refused them as too large or answered "no data" for a stretch of several dates (the halves settle which).
int BrokerSyncCounts.Read rows came from Dhan, int BrokerSyncCounts.Stored are new, int BrokerSyncCounts.Duplicates were stored already, int BrokerSyncCounts.Dropped were unusable rows, int BrokerSyncCounts.Enriched of the int BrokerSyncCounts.Duplicates were completed (a trade stored by an earlier read without its ISIN or charges got them from this one; nothing else of it is touched) and int BrokerSyncCounts.Skipped were not NSE equity trades (by reason in
IReadOnlyDictionary<string, int> BrokerSyncCounts.SkippedByReason). After a trade run the automatic rebuild adds int BrokerSyncCounts.Rebuilt holdings rebuilt, int BrokerSyncCounts.Unchanged already right, int BrokerSyncCounts.NeedsReview holdings with a hand-dated lot that were left alone and the
first int BrokerSyncCounts.MaxNotRebuiltListed of the holdings or securities that were left alone with their reason (int BrokerSyncCounts.NotRebuiltTotal counts all of them). int BrokerSyncCounts.EmptyByNoData counts the windows (or half-windows) that were taken as
empty only because Dhan answered DH-907 ("incorrect parameters or no data present") to the first page: that code means both "nothing there" and "bad request", so the owner can see how often an empty stretch rested on it alone.
`Attempts` is the number of this attempt within the day's occurrence (1 for the scheduled or manual start, 2 to 4 for the quiet retries of ADR 0027), `FailureReason` the plain reason code of a failed run (`unavailable`, `rate_limited`,
`token_expired` ...) and `DeepenedTo` the earliest date an earlier-history read of this run reached. Counts only: no trade or ledger content.

BrokerSyncRunView.description:
A run that reads an account's trades or its ledger. `Kind``trades` or `ledger`; `Trigger``manual`, `scheduled` or `first` (the scheduled backfill of an account never read); `Status``running`,
`succeeded`, `failed` or `skipped`; `From` and `To` the dates it reads. `Counts` says what it did (windows done of total, rows read, new, already stored, unusable (`Counts.Dropped`, and `Counts.DroppedByReason`: how many per reason code, with `Counts.DroppedRows`: the place of the first five - request dates, page, row index and reason, never the row's content), skipped by reason; after a trade run the holdings
rebuilt, unchanged and needing review). `Error` is a short safe text.

BrokerWindowSpan.description: A stretch of whole India dates, DateOnly BrokerWindowSpan.From to DateOnly BrokerWindowSpan.To inclusive, that a run read again (IReadOnlyList<BrokerWindowSpan> BrokerSyncCounts.RereadDone). Dates only: no content of any row.

BucketInput.description: A new custom bucket. The name has 1 to 40 letters, digits, spaces, '_' or '-' and is unique ignoring case.

BucketView.description:
One bucket to pick from. IsAccountDefault is true for the automatic default bucket of an account that has the Portfolio role
(AccountId and AccountName name that account); custom buckets have neither.

CalendarDayView.description:
A date of the trading calendar (ADR 0017 §1). `kind`: holiday · special. A special session has `sessionFrom` and `sessionTo` (`HH:mm`, India time,
