the end exclusive) and `minutes` (its length, the 1-minute bars a complete session has); a holiday has none of the three. `source`: manual · observed · nse.
`status`: confirmed · proposed (`dismissed` days are not listed). `replaces`: set only on a proposal that lies next to a confirmed day (a session seen on a listed
holiday, say) and names that day's kind: the confirmed day stays in force until the owner confirms the proposal (which replaces it) or dismisses it.

CalendarRefreshResult.description:
The answer of a refresh from NSE's public holiday list. It never fails the request: `succeeded` false means the list could not be fetched or read (`message` says why,
nothing changed). Otherwise the counts of the list's holidays that were added, updated, already known and left out (weekends, dates out of range, days the owner
decided or the stored bars contradict).

CalendarView.description:
The trading calendar. `days`: the confirmed holidays and special sessions from `from` to `to` (India dates, both included; default today and a
year on), by date. `proposals`: every proposed day, whatever its date, waiting for Confirm or Dismiss (including proposals that lie next to a confirmed day, marked `replaces`). `nextHoliday`: the first confirmed holiday
today or later (null when none is known).

score.description: The raw score of the trees.

CalibrationPoint.description: One point of the calibration table of a model: a raw score and the probability it maps to.

state.description: The state after the last row (research without rows).

legalNext.description: The states it may move to.

problems.description: Rows that do not add up; empty when consistent.

note.description: What a reader must know: the state is a record; nothing acts on it before paper data and live exist.

CellStateView.description: Where a cell is, replayed from its changelog rows (P6-08).

CellStatsView.description: One row of the cell statistics as the API shows it (P6-01), with the facts a reader needs to judge it (spec honest limits: the basis, the knobs, the evidence flag and the limits text).

CellView.description: One cell (timeframe and side) of a full test: the exit the walk-forward chose and how stable that choice was.

autoApproveTickets.description: The new value of `autonomy.auto_approve_tickets`: ON means tickets the rule allows need no manual approval, OFF means manual approval.

minPWin.description: The least lower-bound P(win), 0.5 to 0.99 (design default 0.58).

maxAutoPerDay.description: The most automatic approvals per planned session, 1 to 20.

password.description: The owner's password, re-entered for THIS change. It is checked on every request (a step-up window opened earlier does not count and is not used up or extended); wrong ones count toward the sign-in lockout.

ChangeAutonomyRequest.description: The body of the autonomy change. The owner is never part of it: the actor comes from the signed-in session.

beforeRef.description: Reference to the thing before, or null.

afterRef.description: Reference to the thing after, or null.

ChangelogEntryView.description: A changelog row as the API shows it (P6-08): what changed, by whom, why, before and after, and the evidence. A revert has long? ChangelogEntryView.RevertsId.

CloneStrategyRequest.description: Body of the clone endpoint: the id of the new strategy; omitted keeps the id (a built-in gets `<ID>_COPY`).

ClonedStrategy.description: A clone (spec P5-01): the text with the new id, the hash of the version it came from (post it as `parentHash` to record the lineage) and the source.

CompletenessCheck.description:
Completeness: the 1-minute bars the trading calendar expects in the window against the ones stored. `missingPercent` is of the expected minutes; `unfillableMinutes` are missing
minutes of sessions a refetch could not fill (a halt, a circuit-locked day): they are a warning, never a failure.

ConnectStartView.description: Where to send the owner's browser to sign in at Dhan (same tab): Dhan's consent login page. The sign-in must come back before ExpiresAt.

ConnectionInput.description: New connection details of an account. Leave ClientId out to keep the current client id.

ConnectionView.description:
The account's connection to Dhan. Status is "not_connected", "connected", "expired" (the expiry has passed — derived when read,
no broker call needed). ExpiresAt is when the token stops working (as Dhan states, otherwise 24 hours after sign-in).
BrokerUserName and BrokerUserId (masked like the client id) are what Dhan reported for the token. LastError is a short safe text (at most
Dhan's error code). The token itself is never returned.

CorporateActionPage.description: A page of corporate actions, newest ex-date first. `pending` is the number of suggestions waiting for a decision over all instruments, whatever the filter.

CorporateActionView.description:
A split or bonus issue of an instrument (ADR 0017 §5). `kind`: split · bonus. `numerator:denominator` (`ratio`): for a split old shares : new shares (1:5 is one share into five), for a bonus
bonus shares : shares held (1:1 is one bonus share for each held). `factor` is the price multiplier for the bars before `exDate` (a 1:5 split 0.2, a 1:1 bonus 0.5). `status`: suggested
(found by the detection, changes nothing yet) · applied (adjusted reads use it) · ignored (declined, kept so it is not suggested again). `source`: manual · detected · csv.
`decidedAt` and `decidedBy` are set once the owner decided (not while suggested). `csvAdjustedThrough`: the date the instrument's loaded CSV files reach (their last bar, in India time; null when
none is loaded). Those files are already adjusted at source, so an action with an ex-date on or before it would adjust their prices twice.

CostBatchPage.description: One page of cost import batches, newest first.

CostBatchView.description: One import of a depository-charges sheet. `Status` is `imported` or `undone`; `ActiveEntries` counts its cost entries that are not voided; `Amount` is the rupees it stored.

CostImportResult.description: What an import of a depository-charges sheet did. `Batch` is null when nothing new was stored. `Imported` entries (`Amount` rupees) were stored; `AlreadyImported` and `AlreadyInLedger` lines were left out; `NamesLearned` names were remembered.

CostUndoResult.description: What undoing a cost batch did: its entries are voided (nothing is deleted). Undoing a batch again is a no-op (`AlreadyUndone`, `Voided` 0).

CreateAccountInput.description:
A new Dhan account. ClientId and Secrets (API key and secret) are required. ApiKeyIssuedOn is the day the API key was generated
(default today, India time).

CreateStrategyRequest.description: Body of `POST /api/lab/strategies`: the text, an optional note (at most 500 characters) and the hash of the version it was cloned from. There is no way to ask for a built-in: the request cannot set it.

CreatedStrategy.description: What a create did (spec P5-01): the version the content has, its hash and parent, and whether a row was written (false: the same content was already stored).

CsvFileCounts.description: The files by state over the whole folder (not narrowed by `state`, but by `q`), and how many cannot be loaded (`unmapped`: unknown, ambiguous or invalid name).

CsvFilePage.description: A page of the folder's files: changed and pending first, then loaded, by name; `total` is the number after the filters.

CsvFilePreview.description:
The dry run of the real reader over one file, nothing written. `verdict`: pass · refused · error (see `message`). `rows` are the data rows, `accepted` the ones that would be stored (`repaired` among them),
`rejected` the others, counted by reason in `rejections` with up to 10 `examples` (line numbers and reasons, never row values). `tradingDays` counts the distinct India dates of the accepted bars.
`wouldLoad`: passes and maps to exactly one instrument. `firstRows`: the first 5 accepted bars. `comparison` is null when the file does not pass or does not map.

CsvFileRow.description:
One file of the CSV folder. `state`: pending · loaded · changed (loaded, but size or modified time differ now). `symbol` is parsed from the name (null for an invalid name),
`mapping`: mapped · unknown · ambiguous · invalidName, `instrument` is set when mapped. `rows`, `firstBar`, `lastBar` (null for a file loaded before the range was recorded) and
`loadedAt` are set for loaded and changed files. `overlapsWith` (loaded and changed files; null for pending ones): the names of the other loaded files of the same instrument that cover part
of the same time — undoing either removes the instrument's CSV bars in the overlap, whichever file wrote them.

CsvInstrumentRef.description: The instrument a file maps to: its id and canonical symbol (`NSE:ABB`).

CsvOverview.description: The CSV folder: the files that match `<SYMBOL>_1m.csv[.gz]`, how many are loaded (unchanged since they were loaded) or pending, the rows loaded so far and when the last file was loaded.

CsvPhase.description:
The CSV phase of a data job (ADR 0016 §4): `Done` of `Total` are files. Rows are counted over all files read in this job. Part of the API
(the job's `csv` block) and stored with the job. `BarsRemoved` is set only by the job that undoes the load of one file (ADR 0017 §6): the CSV bars it removed (null for every other job).

CsvPreviewBar.description: An accepted bar, as the load would store it (after repair), with its start in India time.

CsvPreviewComparison.description:
What loading the file would do to the stored bars of its instrument, in bars: `wouldInsert` (minute not stored yet), `wouldUpdate` (a CSV bar of that minute with other values),
`keepExistingDhan` (a Dhan bar of that minute is kept: CSV never overwrites Dhan) and `unchanged` (same values). Counted over `comparedRows` accepted rows; when the file has more
accepted rows than the request may compare (`sampled`), a spread sample of whole batches is compared and the counts are of that sample, not scaled.

CsvPreviewResult.description: The previews in the order the files were asked for; `rowsRead` and `comparedRows` are the totals of the request (its limits are in the summary of the endpoint).

tickets.description: Tickets in the top K that day.

dayR.description: Sum of R of the day.

cumulativeR.description: Running sum up to and including the day.

CurvePoint.description: One plan-day of a top-K curve (P7-13).

DataAccountView.description: The primary Data account. `status`: connected · expired · notConnected.

DataInstrumentRow.description:
An instrument's coverage. `source`: csv · dhan · mixed (null without bars). `status`: current · behind · empty (tracked, no bars).
`daysBehind` counts trading days (null without bars). `openGaps`: sessions in the last weeks with missing bars that a refetch may still add.

DataJobView.description:
One data job (a run of the pipeline, ADR 0016). `status`: running · succeeded · failed · skipped (a scheduled run that did not start; `error` says why). `trigger`: manual · daily (the scheduled end-of-day run).
`refetchGaps`: the Dhan phase also retried the gaps it had given up on. `currentPhase` (while running): csv · dhan · aggregate · quality. `instrumentId` is set when the job is
about one instrument (a fix action of the Data quality screen). `csvFiles`: the files the CSV step was asked to load (null: every file of the folder). `undoCsvFile`: the file whose load this job undoes
(its `csv` block then reports `barsRemoved` and the message "CSV load of … undone, N bars removed"; the `aggregate` block rebuilds the instrument). `quality` is the data quality phase, present only when the job asked for the step (`runId` names its quality run).
Each phase block has `status` (notRequested · pending · running · succeeded · skipped · failed), `done` of `total` (files, instruments,
instruments), `message` and `code` (why it was skipped or failed) and its counts.

DataNotice.description:
Something about the data pipeline the owner should know, derived from the stored state like the account notices of the bell. `id` includes the situation (a new failed
run or a changed number of open gaps is a new notice, hence unread again). `kind`: data_gaps_open · data_quality_failed (instruments fail the data quality checks: warn within the allowed share, error when the gate blocks the nightly plan) · data_corporate_actions_pending (suggested splits or bonus issues wait for a decision; warn). `severity`: error · warn.

DataRoleInput.description: Switch the Data role. Kind ("primary" or "standby") is required when Enabled is true.

DataRoleView.description: Data role of an account: on/off and which kind.

DematDifference.description: A security whose depository quantity differs from the synced holding's.

DematHeld.description: A security the depository holds that the account has no open holding for.

DematImportResult.description: What an import of a demat holding statement did: it changed no holding. `NamesLearned` names were remembered, `NamesKnown` were remembered already.

DematPreview.description: The preview of a demat holding statement: its securities, how many agree with the synced holdings, the quantity differences, the securities held at Dhan but not synced and the synced holdings missing from the statement (each list at most 200 long, the totals count all) and the names it teaches. Nothing here changes a holding. No notice is raised for these differences; they are shown here only.

DematSynced.description: An open holding of the account that the statement does not list.

DetectionResult.description: What a detection run did: `instruments` looked at, `candidates` found, `suggested` new suggestions stored (the others were known already, ignored ones included) and `pending` suggestions now waiting.

DhanOverview.description:
The Dhan Data API phase: the primary Data account (null when there is none), whether a fetch can run now (`canFetch`) and, when not, why
(`reason` in words, `reasonCode` data.dhan_not_available · data.dhan_not_connected), the settings, and the last successful fetch (time and bars added).

DhanPhase.description:
The Dhan phase of a data job (ADR 0016 §2, §7): `Done` of `Total` are instruments. `Bars` are the 1-minute bars Dhan returned;
`Rejected` are bars that did not lie on an IST minute inside a session or broke the row rules; `OverlapCompared` and
`OverlapMismatched` compare the overlap with the bars already stored (tolerance 0.05 %). `GapsFound` counts the instrument-sessions with missing bars
this phase planned to refetch or found still incomplete, `GapsFilled` those that now have all their bars and `GapsUnfillable` those a refetch added nothing to
(ADR 0017 §3). Part of the API (the job's `dhan` block).

DhanRedirectView.description: The redirect URL to register with the Dhan app, exactly as shown: `{PublicBaseUrl}/api/brokers/dhan/callback`.

DividendBadRow.description: A row that cannot be imported: the line of the file it starts on and why.

DividendBatchPage.description: One page of import batches, newest first.

DividendBatchView.description: One import of a dividend file. `Status` is `imported` or `undone`; `ActiveDividends` counts its dividends that are not voided; `Amount` is the rupees it stored.

DividendBeforeFirstLot.description: The dividends to be added that are dated before the account's first lot (`FirstLotDate`; null: the account has no lot): the net XIRR cannot count an inflow before the first outflow — read the earlier trade history.

DividendCandidate.description: A holding that fits an ambiguous scrip name.

DividendChoice.description:
What the owner decided for a scrip name of the file: exactly one of `HoldingId` (one of the account's holdings), `InstrumentId` (an NSE share or ETF of the instrument list) and `None` (keep the dividends unallocated). It applies to every
row with that name. `Name` is the scrip name as the file wrote it or the item's `NameKey` (best: send the `NameKey`); either way it is reduced to the key names are compared by (case, punctuation and company suffixes
ignored), so two spellings of one company are one scrip. Several choices for one scrip are fine when they agree (one is made of them) and a 400 when they disagree. With `Remember` the choice is saved as an alias, so later files with that name need no question.

DividendFileSummary.description:
What was in the file. `Rows` are the data rows (empty lines do not count), `Parsed` the valid rows (`ParsedAmount` their rupees), `Repeated` the valid rows that repeat an earlier row of the file identically (counted once; listed in
`IdenticalRepeats`, at most 200), `Distinct` the rows left (`Parsed - Repeated`). Of the distinct rows: `AlreadyImported` are stored already, `PossibleDuplicates` equal a dividend you typed in, and `ToAdd` would be stored,
among them `NeedsMatch` (no holding or instrument found: stored unallocated with the file's name) and `Ambiguous` (more than one holding fits: stored unallocated unless you choose). `Bad` lists the first 200 bad rows (line, reason);
`BadTotal` counts all of them.

DividendImportResult.description:
What an import did. `Batch` is null when nothing new was stored. `Imported` dividends (`Amount` rupees) were stored: `Allocated` to a holding, `InstrumentOnly` with an instrument but no holding, `Unallocated` with the
file's name only. `AlreadyImported` rows were stored before, `PossibleDuplicatesSkipped` equal a dividend you typed in and were not ticked, `AliasesSaved` names were remembered.

DividendInput.description:
A dividend typed in by the owner: for a holding (`HoldingId`; the account is then the holding's) or, left unallocated, for an account (`AccountId` alone). `PayDate` is the day the money was credited (not in the future),
`Amount` the rupees received (above 0, to the paisa), `PerShare` optional (above 0), `Note` optional plain text (at most 200 characters). The same account, holding, date and amount twice is allowed (two genuine payments) but the second asks
for a confirmation: `409 portfolio.possible_duplicate`, repeat with `Confirm` true.

DividendMatchView.description:
What a row's scrip name means. `Kind` is the rule that decided: `alias` (remembered), `isin`, `symbol` (the file's columns), `name` (equal names), `contains` (part of a name), `master` (a share of the instrument list that
is not held), `choice` (your pick in an import) or `none`. With a `HoldingId` the dividend belongs to that holding; with only an `InstrumentId` it keeps the instrument, ISIN and symbol but no holding; with neither it is
unallocated. `Candidates` (two or more) are the holdings an ambiguous name fits: nothing is guessed. `Symbol`, `Isin` and `Name` are those of the holding or instrument (plain text).

DividendPage.description: One page of dividends, newest first (pay date), voided ones included and flagged.

DividendPreviewItem.description:
A distinct row of the file. `Name` is the scrip name as the file wrote it (plain text, untrusted); `NameKey` is the name reduced to what the server compares names by (case, punctuation and company suffixes ignored,
the ampersand read as and): two spellings of one company have one `NameKey`, so group the rows that need a choice by it and key the choices by it. `Status`: `new`, `imported` (stored already), `possible_duplicate`, `needs_match`, `ambiguous`.
`Warnings`: `amount_mismatch` (per share × quantity differs from the amount paid by more than ₹0.01; the amount paid is used), `before_first_lot` (the date is before the account's first lot, so the net XIRR cannot count it),
`partial_name_match` (matched by part of the name: check it).

DividendPreviewReport.description:
The preview of a dividend file import — nothing is stored. `Format` is `dividends`. `Items` are the distinct rows in file order. `Digest` fingerprints what is shown; an import must send it back, and answers
`409 portfolio.preview_stale` when holdings, aliases or dividends changed since.

DividendRepeat.description: A payment that appears more than once, identically, in the file: counted once. `Lines` are the lines of its occurrences (at most 10 listed).

DividendSuggestionPage.description:
The suggested dividends of an account: its ledger entries of class `dividend` the owner has not accepted or dismissed, newest first. Dhan's documented ledger has no entry for an ordinary dividend, so the list is usually empty. The entries'
`Description` and `Narration` are Dhan's free text: untrusted, show as plain text.

DividendTotals.description: What an import would add: the number of dividends and rupees (the rows that are to be added — not stored yet, not possible duplicates) and the same by pay year.

DividendUndoResult.description: What undoing a batch did: its dividends are voided (nothing is deleted). Undoing a batch again is a no-op (`AlreadyUndone`, `Voided` 0).

DividendUploadForm.description: The multipart form of the dividend preview and import, for the API contract only (the request is read by DividendUploads). `AccountId` is the account, `File` the dividend list (CSV). For the import also `Digest` (required: the digest of the preview), `Choices` and `IncludeDuplicates`. A form field is text: send `Choices` and `IncludeDuplicates` as JSON text (`JSON.stringify` of a `DividendChoice[]` and of a list of line numbers of possible duplicates to import anyway); the types here say what the JSON holds.

DividendView.description:
A dividend. `HoldingId` is null for an unallocated one; `Symbol` and `Isin` are the holding's (or the matched instrument's) at the time. `Source` is `manual` or `csv` (read from a dividend file, ADR 0028). A dividend from a file
has its import's `BatchId`, the file's `Quantity` (shares) when it had one and, when it belongs to no holding, the file's `ScripName` (plain text, untrusted). A voided dividend does not count.

DividendYearTotal.description: Rows and rupees of one year.

DpCounts.description: The lines of a depository-charges sheet by what happens to them. `OffMarket` counts (among the others) the lines of type off-market.

DpLineView.description: A line of a depository-charges sheet. `Status`: `new` (stored by an import), `zero` (costs nothing), `buy_side` (not charged), `already_imported`, `already_in_ledger` (Dhan's ledger has a charge of that amount that day). `Side` is `buy`, `sell` or `other`.

DpPreview.description: The preview of a depository-charges sheet: the lines (at most 300 listed, `LinesTotal` counts all), their counts, the rupees an import would add to the account's costs and the names it teaches.

Drawdown.description:
The largest peak-to-trough fall of a NAV series: `Pct` is a percent number (12.5 means it fell 12.5 %) from the peak on `From` to the low on `To`. A series that never falls (flat or rising)
gives 0 and no dates.

EodOverview.description:
The scheduled end-of-day run (ADR 0017 §2) as set on the Services screen (ADR 0018): `enabled` (the service is not paused), `timeIst` (`HH:mm`, India time; empty when the schedule has no time of its own),
`nextRunAt` (the next scheduled start; null when paused or none ahead), `lastRun` (the latest automatic data job, null before the first) and `scheduleWords` (the schedule in words).

EodRunView.description:
An automatic (scheduled) run as the Data screen shows it. `status`: running · succeeded · failed · skipped; `message` is the reason a run failed or was skipped
(for example the Data account was not connected). `trigger` is always `daily` here.

EvidenceView.description: The out-of-sample numbers a verdict was judged on. A number that is not finite (an infinite profit factor) is null; the reason of its gate says it in words.

ExecutionView.description: How a service is run: retries (0–5 after a failed attempt), the timeout of an attempt in minutes (1–240), whether a missed run is made up for when the application starts, and whether a failure raises a notice in the bell.

experimentKey.description: The hash that identifies the experiment.

holdOutStart.description: First day of the hold-out that was not read, or null when none was kept.

trials.description: The experiments of the last 30 days when it was judged, itself included.

requiredImprovementR.description: The improvement required, mean R per trade.

pooledBaselineMeanR.description: Pooled mean R of the baseline over the used folds, or null.

baselineTotalR.description: Total R of the baseline after the live gap.

expectedLiveGapR.description: The live gap assumed, R per trade.

compareMs.description: Milliseconds spent reading both runs and judging them (measured); the replay is not included and not measured.

reasons.description: Why it is not better; empty when better.

reportText.description: The report with its honest limits; empty in a list.

parameters.description: The rules used; empty in a list.

ExperimentView.description: An experiment as the API shows it (P6-11, ADR 0072). The report text and the parameters are empty in a list and filled for one experiment.

FacetCount.description: A filter value and how many active instruments have it.

feature.description: The feature name, or `f<index>` when the catalog of the model is not the current one.

meanAbsContribution.description: For a model the mean absolute contribution over its training rows; for one score the signed contribution.

FeatureImportanceView.description: The weight of one feature in a model or in one score: a path-based contribution in raw-score units (not exact, not SHAP).

FirstImportInput.description:
Optional per-holding dates for the first import that happens when the portfolio settings are saved (ADR 0013). Without rows, every holding Dhan lists is
imported dated with the first import date (flagged default-date); a row (key from `holdings/preview`, acquisition date) overrides the date of its holding.
At most 5000 rows. Used only when the account is connected to Dhan and has no holdings yet.

FirstImportView.description:
What a first import did. Status: "imported" (the holdings were created; the counts say how many), "skipped" (the account already has holdings, nothing was
imported), "deferred" (the account is not connected to Dhan, or the Portfolio role is off: the first sync imports every holding, dated FirstImportDate) or
"failed" (the settings were saved but the import was not: ErrorCode is `portfolio.import_failed`, Cause the code of the reason, for example
`portfolio.not_connected`, `portfolio.sync_running`; Message says what to do; save again or press Sync now to retry). Imported counts holdings created, DefaultDated those
among them dated by the first import date, AlreadyImported keys the account had already, Unknown keys Dhan no longer lists. Redated counts the lots that
followed a changed first import date (imported lots still on the default date; they stay flagged as such), RedateSkipped the ones that could not follow
because they were closed before the new date; both are 0 when the date did not change or the account has no holdings (ADR 0015).

FreshnessCheck.description: Freshness against the trading calendar: the last bar and the last closed session; `daysBehind` counts trading days.

FullPeriodView.description: A full-period (in-sample) figure of one candidate in one cell. It is exploration and never reaches the verdict.

GapRow.description:
A session of an instrument with missing 1-minute bars (ADR 0017 §3). `date` is the India date, `expected` the bars a complete session has (from the trading
calendar), `found` what is stored, `attempts` how often a refetch was made. `status`: open · filled · unfillable (a refetch added nothing).
`lastAttemptAt` is the latest refetch (null before the first), `detectedAt` when the gap was found.

GapsOverview.description:
How many instrument-sessions are in each state (the Dhan phase's gap table): `open` (missing bars a refetch may still add), `unfillable` (a refetch added
nothing), `filled`; `lastDetectedAt` is when a gap was last found (null while there never was one).

GateView.description: One gate of a verdict as served (spec P5-03, P5-04); `Actual` is null when it is not finite.

points.description: One per plan-day, by date then plan.

GradeCurve.description: The top-K curve by rank: its points day by day and its totals.

curves.description: Top-1, top-3, top-5 and top-all by rank over primary and reserve tickets.

decisions.description: Approved, modified, rejected, lapsed and undecided (primary and reserve tickets only).

comparisons.description: Did the reserve, the rejection and the owner's refusals help.

GradeReportData.description: The numbers of doc 10 section 8 over a set of graded tickets (P7-13, ADR 0090).

meanR.description: Mean R per triggered ticket; null with none.

winRate.description: Share of triggered tickets with R above zero; null with none.

note.description: The honest note on the sample size; null when the sample reaches int GradeReport.IndicativeBelow.

GradeStats.description: The figures of a set of graded tickets (P7-13). R is summed over the graded (triggered) tickets only; the others add nothing and are counted.

meanDifference.description: Mean R of the first minus mean R of the second; null when either has no triggered ticket.

verdict.description: first_better, second_better, equal or not_enough_data. Never a claim of significance.

GroupComparison.description: Two sets compared by mean R per triggered ticket (P7-13): what the second would have added or avoided.

GroupPart.description: The value of the holdings of a group that fall in one part of the second dimension (an account for sectors, a sector for accounts); the parts sum to the group's value.

HistoryBenchmark.description:
The benchmark of a history. `State` is `ok` (the benchmark lines are filled) or `unavailable` with the `Reason` in words. `Symbol` is the canonical symbol and `Name` the display name of the index (null when the master list has
no such index). `Tracked`: tracking is on; `HasBars`: 1-minute bars are stored (the day bars follow when the aggregates are built). A screen offers "Track the benchmark" when it is unavailable and not tracked.
`AsOf` is the date of the last index close the benchmark lines were valued at (null when unavailable): the index has no live quote, so the benchmark lines end there and a live point of today (portfolio at today's prices) has no benchmark value.

HistoryCoverage.description:
How much of the open holdings the history covers: `Holdings` open holdings, `Covered` of them have stored day bars, `Unpriced` have none (not tracked, not in the instrument master, or bars not fetched yet:
they are left out and never valued at zero). `LateStart` counts covered holdings whose bars begin after their earliest lot, so part of their history is missing.

HistoryPoint.description:
One day of the portfolio history (rupees; `Nav` and `BenchmarkNav` start at 100). `Value` is what the lots held that day were worth at the day's close (adjusted prices), `Invested` what
they cost. `BenchmarkValue` is the same cash flows put into the benchmark index; it and `BenchmarkNav` are null when the benchmark has no history for the series.

HoldingGroup.description:
One group. Key is the account id, bucket id, sector name or basket id, or `~none` for the sector "Unclassified" and the basket "No basket". Holdings counts every holding of the group in the scope;
Unpriced the open ones without a usable price. DayChangeExcluded counts the open holdings left out of the day change. Parts is set only when the request had a `stackBy`. Income is the group's dividends and trade
charges and the net returns (ADR 0026), null when none is recorded; a group by account also holds the account's own dividends and costs (those of no holding). The group with the key `~unallocated` (name "Unallocated", no holdings,
no value) is added last when dividends and costs belong to no group, so that the columns add up to the total.

HoldingGroupTotal.description: The scope's totals, computed once over every holding of the scope (for basket groupings this is not the sum of the groups). WeightPct is 100 when the scope has a value. Income includes the dividends and costs of no holding.

HoldingGroups.description:
The groups of the scope. By is `account`, `bucket`, `sector` or `basket`; Additive is false for baskets (a holding is in every basket that contains it, so the groups overlap). StackBy is the second dimension of the
parts, when asked for. At most 200 groups are returned.

HoldingLots.description: The lots of a holding, open lots first (oldest first), then closed ones.

HoldingPage.description: One page of holdings (Total counts all matches).

HoldingRebuildResult.description: The rebuild of one holding's lots: with `DryRun` only what it would do; otherwise `Applied` says whether the lots were replaced (only an `ok` rebuild is).

HoldingRow.description:
One holding. Status is "open" or "closed". Mapped is false when the holding is not in the instrument master (InstrumentId and CanonicalSymbol are
then null). LotCount counts open lots; EarliestAcquiredOn is the oldest open lot's date; UsesDefaultDate is true when any open lot has the
import's default date. Returns cover all lots (closed lots add to RealisedPnl and to the XIRR).
PreviousClose is the previous session's close as the last quote reported it (null until a quote gave one). DayChange (rupees) and DayChangePct (percent number) are
against it, for an open, priced holding with a previous close; otherwise both are null and the holding is left out of the summary's day change. PriceAt is the time of
LastPrice (the same instant as LastPriceAt) and PriceSource says where the price came from: "sync" (the holdings list at the last sync), "quote" (a market quote) or "live" (a tick of the live feed).
Income is the holding's dividends and trade charges and the net returns that include them (ADR 0026); null when nothing is recorded for the holding. It does not change with the price, except the two total return percentages: the
browser works those out again at a live price from Returns.RealisedPnl, Returns.Pnl, Returns.Invested and Income's Dividends and Charges.

HoldingsSummary.description:
Totals over the holdings of the filter (all accounts that count in totals, one account, one bucket). DefaultDateLots counts open lots that
still have the import's default date. UnpricedCount counts open holdings without a usable price: they are left out of Returns (invested, value, P&L, XIRR). ValuationDate is the day the values are as of (today in India).
DayChange (rupees) is the sum of the day changes of the included open holdings and DayChangePct (percent number) is that sum over the sum of qty x previous close of the same holdings; both are null when no
holding is included. DayChangeExcluded counts the open holdings left out (no previous close or no usable price). PricesAsOf holds the oldest and the newest price time of the open priced holdings.
BenchmarkXirr (percent number) is the XIRR of the same cash flows put into the benchmark index (Nifty 50 by default, ADR 0020 §2), Alpha the portfolio's XIRR minus it in percentage points; BenchmarkState is "ok", "unavailable" (the index has no history
from the first cash flow: track it and run Update data), "insufficient" (the same reasons as for XIRR) or "n_m" (beyond ±1,000 %). BenchmarkXirr and Alpha are null unless their rates are meaningful (Alpha also needs the portfolio's XirrState "ok").
BenchmarkAsOf is the date of the index close the benchmark was valued at: the index has no live quote, so on a trading day before its bar is fetched it is the previous close while the portfolio is valued at today's prices. AlphaBasis says which
it is when Alpha is set: "last_close" (portfolio and index are both as of their last close) or "live_vs_last_close" (the portfolio at prices of a later trading day than the index close, so the alpha includes the day's move of the portfolio only).
Alpha compares price returns: the gross XIRR and the index's price index, both before dividends and charges (ADR 0026). Income holds the dividends and costs of the scope and the net returns (null when nothing is recorded): for the whole portfolio or
an account (no bucket) it includes the dividends not allocated to a holding and the ledger's costs, for a bucket only its holdings'.

code.description: Stable machine-readable error code, e.g. auth.invalid_credentials, auth.locked, auth.session_expired, auth.csrf_invalid, auth.step_up_required, accounts.not_found, accounts.invalid (field errors in "errors"), accounts.conflict, accounts.app_not_configured, accounts.broker_error (502), accounts.connect_mismatch, accounts.consent_limit (429), accounts.connect_expired, accounts.connect_cancelled, portfolio.not_connected, portfolio.sync_running, portfolio.confirmation_required and portfolio.confirmation_stale (409, with listedHoldings, openHoldings and wouldClose), portfolio.conflict (409), portfolio.invalid, portfolio.not_found, portfolio.lot_from_trade (409), portfolio.preview_stale (409, with report), services.not_found (404), services.invalid (400, with issues), services.revision_changed (409), services.already_running (409), services.read_only (409).

retryAfterSeconds.description: Present on auth.locked, auth.rate_limited and accounts.consent_limit: seconds until a new attempt may succeed.

openHoldings.description: Present on portfolio.confirmation_required and portfolio.confirmation_stale: how many holdings the account has open.

listedHoldings.description: Present on portfolio.confirmation_required and portfolio.confirmation_stale: how many holdings Dhan listed.

issues.description: Present on services.invalid: every error of the refused schedule - the service it is about (serviceId; absent for the service of the request), the field (a dotted path like the request, e.g. schedule.time, retries, parameters.x), severity (error), a stable code and the text.

report.description: Present on portfolio.preview_stale: the fresh preview of the file, in the shape of the response of POST /api/portfolio/trades/preview (TradePreviewReport).

wouldClose.description: Present on portfolio.confirmation_required: how many of them the sync would close because Dhan no longer lists them.

HypothesisStepView.description: One row of a hypothesis's history.

state.description: proposed, approved, running, judged, accepted, rejected or expired.

cellKey.description: The cell it is about, or null.

baselineValue.description: The value in the baseline run.

experimentId.description: The experiment that judged it, once judged.

reason.description: The reason of the newest move.

nextStates.description: The states it may move to.

history.description: Every step, oldest first; empty in a list.

note.description: What an accepted hypothesis does and does not do.

HypothesisView.description: A hypothesis as the API shows it (P6-10, ADR 0076): the newest row of its log, with the legal next states and, for one hypothesis, its history.

ImportCorporateActionsResult.description:
The outcome of a CSV import (or its preview). `lines`: data lines read; `importable`: new valid actions; `imported`: written (0 for a preview); `duplicates`: lines that repeat an action
that exists (any status) or an earlier line; `invalid`: lines with a problem (the first 50 in `errors`, among them lines that clash with an applied action of the other kind on the same day);
`unknownSymbols`: symbols that match no listed instrument (never guessed). `adjustsCsvTwice`: how many of the importable lines have an ex-date on or before the date their instrument's loaded
CSV files reach, listed in `warnings` (the first 50); an import (not a preview) with such lines needs `acknowledgeCsvAdjusted=true`, else 409 `data.csv_already_adjusted`.

ImportFileError.description: Why a file could not be read or imported: `portfolio.invalid` (`Field``file`), `portfolio.wrong_file_kind` (an unknown shape; the message lists the accepted kinds), `portfolio.preview_stale`, `portfolio.other_account`, `portfolio.sync_running`, `portfolio.conflict`.

ImportFilePreview.description:
What a file is and what importing it would do — nothing is stored. `Kind`: `global_transaction_report`, `dp_charges`, `demat_holding`, `pnl_report`, `trades` (a tradebook with a buy/sell column), `dividends`, `tradebook_without_sides`,
`statement`, `unknown`. `Supported` is true when the file can be imported here. A file that belongs on another screen has `RouteTo` (`dividends`); one that cannot be imported has a `Message` saying why; a file that cannot be read has an `Error`. Of
the blocks only the one of the kind is set: `Trades` (the tradebook preview: global transaction report and tradebook) with `Bill` beside it for the global transaction report, `Costs` (depository charges), `Demat`. `Digest` fingerprints what is shown;
an import sends it back.

ImportFileResult.description:
What importing one file did. `Status`: `imported` (something was stored), `nothing_new` (nothing to store: the file is imported already), `not_supported` (the kind cannot be imported; `Message` says why), `rejected` (`Error` says why; a
`portfolio.preview_stale` error comes with the fresh `Preview` and nothing was stored). Of the results only the one of the kind is set: `Trades` (global transaction report and tradebook), `Costs`, `Demat`. `AliasesSaved` counts the choices remembered.

ImportLineError.description: A line of an imported text that could not be used, with the reason (no free text from the file is repeated).

ImportLineWarning.description:
A valid line whose ex-date is on or before the date the instrument's loaded CSV files reach (`csvAdjustedThrough`): importing it would adjust those already adjusted prices twice.
`symbol` is the canonical symbol (`NSE:ABB`).

ImportPreview.description: What Dhan holds for the account, nothing saved. DefaultDate is the account's first import date (2025-01-01 until the owner chooses another).

ImportPreviewResponse.description: The previews of the files of one request, in the order they were sent.

ImportRowInput.description: One holding to import (a key from the preview). AcquiredOn left out means "use the first import date" (the lot is then flagged).

ImportRunResponse.description: The results of the files of one request, in the order they were sent.

ImportSummary.description: The counts every kind of file has. `Rows` are the data rows, `Valid` the rows that can be used, `ToAdd` what an import would store, `AlreadyImported` what is stored already, `Skipped` the valid rows left out (by reason in the kind's own block), `Bad` the rows that cannot be used. `From`/`To` are the period the report says it covers.

ImportWarning.description: A notice about a file. `Code`: `other_account` (the report's client code differs from that of the reports imported into the account before; the account remembers a hash of the first code, never the code), `charges_differ_from_footer`, `needs_match` (`Count` names that could not be tied to a security), `partial_name_match`, `negative_charges`, `value_not_reproduced`, `covered_by_dhan`, `totals_differ`, `bad_rows`, `holdings_differ` (a demat statement and the synced holdings differ; nothing is changed), `notice_only` (the file is recognised and not imported).

IncomeView.description:
What a scope (a holding, a group, an account, the portfolio) received and paid beyond its price return (ADR 0026, P2-14). Money is rupees, percentages are percent numbers (16.1 = 16.1 %), dates are India dates. `Dividends` are the
dividends the owner entered (not voided) and `Charges` the trade charges of the stored trades plus, for an account and the portfolio only, the ledger's costs of the account as such (DP charges, annual maintenance, delayed-payment interest ...;
never the costs of trades, which the trade rows already carry). `LedgerCharges` is that ledger part of `Charges` (0 when the account has none; null when the scope does not include account-level items: a holding, a bucket), so the screen can show
the ledger's costs apart from the charges of trades. `Unallocated` is the part of the dividends not allocated to a holding (set for an account and the portfolio only, otherwise null). `TotalReturnPct` is (realised + unrealised +
dividends) over invested, `NetTotalReturnPct` the same minus the charges; both are null when nothing is invested or the scope has no usable price. `NetXirr` is the XIRR of the lot cash flows plus the dividends (in) and the charges (out) on
their dates, with `NetXirrState` as for the gross XIRR (`ok`, `insufficient`, `n_m`, `no_data`, `no_price`).
Only what was entered or read is counted, and the dates say from when each source is known (null: the source has nothing for the scope): `DividendsFrom` is the first dividend the owner entered, `TradeChargesFrom` the first stored trade that
carries charges (trades read before charges were stored, and CSV or manual trades, carry none — so a trade without charges is "unknown", not "free"), `LedgerChargesFrom` the first ledger date stored. `ChargesFrom` is the later of
`TradeChargesFrom` and `LedgerChargesFrom` when both exist, otherwise the one that does. `CoverageFrom` is the LATER start of the sources that exist for the scope: the date from which every kind of income that is counted at all is known, so
the net figures are never presented as complete from before any of their sources begins. The whole object is null when the scope has no dividend and no charge recorded.

InstrumentBars.description:
The latest bars of an instrument and timeframe, newest first. `adjustment` is set only when the read asked for adjusted prices (`adjusted=true`): the bars then have the open, high, low and close multiplied by
the cumulative factor of the corporate actions applied after their date, rounded to 4 decimals, and the volume divided by it; the block says which actions and what factor (see AdjustmentView).

InstrumentBasketView.description: A basket that holds an instrument now; `since` = when it was added.

InstrumentDetail.description: Everything the master list knows about an instrument.

InstrumentPage.description: One page of search results (`total` counts all matches).

InstrumentPrice.description:
The latest known price of an instrument: `lastPrice` at `priceAt` (the time of the exchange's tick for `live`, the time of the quote for `quote`, the time of the sync for `sync`; UTC) and where it came from:
`live` (the live feed), `quote` (the 5-minute quote poll) or `sync` (the broker's holdings list). The same values as `lastPrice`, `priceAt` and `priceSource` of the holdings list. An older price never follows a newer one
for the same instrument; a client that gets one anyway ignores it.

InstrumentSummary.description: A row of the master list. `type`: share · etf · index · future.

LabCounts.description: The counts of a finished run: the instruments asked for and replayed, the ones skipped, and the trades (closed and open at the end of the data).

LabInstrument.description: One instrument of a Lab run's universe.

LabProblem.description: One located problem of a run, with the stage that found it.

LabProgressView.description: Where a running run is: instruments done of instruments in total (0 and 0 outside the quick test).

LabReportView.description:
The report of a finished full or robust test (spec P5-06, doc 11 §4), built from the stored result only. `NotIncluded` names the sections of doc 11 §4 that the stored result cannot fill, so nothing is invented. `Summary` is a deterministic
template over the numbers above, not an assistant text.

LabRunFinished.description: Client event `labRunFinished` (spec P5-02, D5): the last event of a run, with its final state.

LabRunProgress.description: Client event `labRunProgress` (spec P5-02, D5): a run entered a stage or advanced in it. `done` and `total` count instruments in the quick test and are 0 elsewhere.

LabRunView.description:
A Lab run as the API serves it (spec P5-02, Contract): the same data the hub's events carry, so a missed event costs nothing. `verdict` is always null in this slice (P5-03); `labels` carry the cost basis, the sample and the line that a
quick test is exploration, not a verdict (D6).

LabStageLog.description: One entry of the stage log: when a stage began and ended and how many problems it found.

LabStrategyRef.description: The strategy version a run tests.

LabUniverse.description:
The universe of a Lab run as it was resolved when the run was posted (spec P5-02, D2): the basket changes later, the run keeps the list. Requested is the number of members before the quick-test sample;
Sampled says the list was cut to the limit by the seeded shuffle of Seed.

LabVerdictView.description: The verdict of a full test with everything it rests on (spec P5-04): outcome, gates, limits, the cells and the exploration block.

LabWindow.description: The India dates a run replays, inclusive.

LastDataJobs.description: The latest job in which each phase ran to an end (null when none did yet).

cellRows.description: Rows in the newest cell-statistics snapshot (all windows).

cellsAsOf.description: The as-of date of that snapshot, or null before the first computation.

LearningOverviewView.description: What the Learning screen needs first (P6-18, ADR 0080): counts and the newest verdicts of the stored learning records. Read from the stores; no statistic is computed and no model is scored.

LedgerClassTotal.description: The entries of one class in the period and their signed total.

LedgerEntryView.description:
A ledger entry. `Class` is `funds_in`, `funds_out`, `dividend`, `charges` or `other`; `Amount` is signed (credit minus debit). `Description` and `Narration` are Dhan's free text (untrusted: show as plain text).
`Source` is `broker` (read from Dhan's ledger) or `import` (a cost imported from a downloaded report, such as the depository-charges sheet, which can be undone).

LedgerPage.description:
One page of the ledger, newest first, and the totals of every class for the period (`from` to `to`, whatever class is filtered). `CoverageFrom` is the earliest date of any ledger entry stored for the account, whatever the filters
(null: none stored): the ledger's costs are known from this date on, which reading from an earlier date can move back (ADR 0026).

LedgerRowView.description: One ledger row as the API shows it (`window` is the posted window).

LedgerView.description: The ledger of a family, the number of variants in it and the factor the gates are tightened by now (1 when the adjustment is off).

LessonStepView.description: One row of a lesson's history.

experimentId.description: The linked or resolved experiment, or null.

experimentOutcome.description: Outcome of the experiment the result was read from.

beforeMeanR.description: Pooled mean R before (baseline), or null.

afterMeanR.description: Pooled mean R after (candidate), or null.

reason.description: The reason of the newest move.

nextStates.description: The states it may move to.

history.description: Every step, oldest first; empty in a list.

note.description: What a lesson does and does not do.

LessonView.description: A lesson as the API shows it (P6-16, ADR 0078): the newest row of its log, with the legal next states and, for one lesson, its history.

LiveFeedStatus.description:
The state of the live feed as the screen needs it: hub event `feedStatus` (pushed on connect, on a change of `state` or `subscribed`, and every 15 seconds) and the body of `GET /api/live/status` (the fallback when the hub is not connected).
`state` is the feed's own word: `connected` (streaming), `idle` (connected, nothing to follow), `connecting`, `reconnecting`, `closed` (outside its window), `paused` (the owner paused the service), `no_token`, `token_refused`,
`flapping`; or `not_running` when the feed reports nothing (never started, stopped, crashed: no heartbeat in the last 60 seconds). `subscribed` is the number of instruments the feed follows (0 unless it reports); `lastTickAt` the exchange
time of its latest tick of any instrument (UTC), null when none yet.

LiveScope.description:
What a Portfolio screen asks the hub to follow (argument of `Subscribe`, ADR 0024 §7): the prices of the instruments of these holdings are pushed, nothing else.
`accountId` and `bucketId` are the screen's scope, with the meaning they have for `GET /api/holdings/summary`: without `accountId` every open holding of the accounts that count in totals, with it every open holding of that account
(any account that is not archived); `bucketId` narrows either to one bucket. This is the set the tiles and the group rows are made of.
`holdingIds` are the holdings the screen shows (rows of the grid, the open drawer); they are added to the scope's holdings even when the scope would not include them (an account that does not count in totals, a filter applied on the screen only).
At most 1000 are read; holdings that are closed or have no instrument are ignored. Leave `accountId`, `bucketId` and `holdingIds` null or empty for all accounts that count in totals.
The server turns holdings into instruments; the messages carry instrument ids (as `instrumentId` of the holdings list). A second `Subscribe` replaces the first.

LongTermLot.description: A profitable open lot that turns 12 months old soon (the `long_term_soon` rule): `LongTermOn` is the date it is 12 months old, `DaysLeft` the days until then, `GainPct` its unrealised gain in percent (null for a lot that cost nothing, for example bonus shares: the gain is then the whole value and has no percentage).

LotDateInput.description: Sets the acquisition date of a lot (between 1990-01-01 and today, India).

LotRow.description:
A lot of a holding with its own figures: Invested is its cost, Value is its value now (open) or its sale proceeds (closed), Pnl the difference.
Status is "open" or "closed"; Source "import", "added" or "manual". Estimated: the sale price is the last price a sync saw.

ManualTradeInput.description:
A trade typed in by the owner: for a holding (`HoldingId`) or for a security of an account (`AccountId` and `Symbol` and/or `Isin`, which must be an NSE share or ETF of the master list). `Side` buy or sell, the date not in the
future, `Quantity` a whole number above 0, `Price` above 0, `Charges` optional (0).

MembersOrderInput.description: Every member of the basket exactly once, in the wanted order.

MissingMinute.description: A missing minute: the India date and the minute (`HH:mm`).

reportText.description: The validation report with its honest limits.

importance.description: The features by weight, largest first.

limits.description: The sentences that must be read with the model.

ModelDetailView.description: A model with everything the registry keeps about it (P6-07).

sha256.description: The hash of the model file.

trainingSetId.description: The training set it was made from.

note.description: What a reader must know about the fit, or null.

fitRows.description: Rows the trees were fitted on.

calibrationRows.description: Rows the calibration was fitted on.

trainRows.description: Development rows it was trained on.

holdOutStart.description: First day of the hold-out that was not read, or null when none was kept.

foldsBeatingBoth.description: Folds in which it beat both baselines.

pooledEcePp.description: Pooled expected calibration error in percentage points.

reasons.description: Why it is not eligible; empty when eligible.

role.description: The current role: challenger, champion or retired.

mayBeChampion.description: The record allows the role champion: an Eligible verdict, a hold-out kept, enough folds and the trials of the registry.

ModelView.description: A registered model as the API shows it (P6-07, ADR 0070): what made it, what the harness said about it and its current role. No model bytes.

MonteCarloView.description: The bootstrap of the out-of-sample trades; the seed is text (a 64-bit number).

NameLearning.description: Names a depository or demat file teaches: `Known` are remembered already, `New` would be remembered by an import.

OfficialDailyCheck.description: The comparison of the derived daily bar with the broker's official daily candle: not available until official daily candles are fetched.

OpeningQtyView.description: The quantity the lots count as opening (the shares the trades do not explain): now, and after the rebuild. Null where it cannot be told (no holding, or a quantity that is not whole after a split or bonus).

count.description: How many of the newest records have it.

OverviewCount.description: A name and how many records carry it (P6-18).

label.description: Role of a model, knob of an experiment, kind of a changelog row.

verdict.description: The stored verdict, outcome or state after.

detail.description: One line of the stored numbers.

OverviewHeadline.description: The newest record of one kind, as the overview shows it (P6-18): what it is, the verdict that was stored and one line of the stored numbers. Nothing here is computed.

counted.description: Records counted: at most the newest int GetLearningOverviewHandler.CountLimit.

truncated.description: True when there may be more records than were counted.

split.description: The count by role (models), outcome (experiments) or state (hypotheses, lessons); only names that occur.

oneOf.description: The newest record, or null when none is stored.
For models, the current champion; null otherwise or when there is none.

OverviewSection.description: One kind of learning record in the overview (P6-18): how many were counted, the split by role, outcome or state, and the newest record.

ParameterSensitivityView.description: The sweep of one parameter and its judgement (`stable`, `fragile`, `no_base_edge`, `inconclusive`).

ParameterView.description: A parameter of a service with its schema: `kind` integer · number · boolean, the bounds of a number, the current value and the default.

itemId.description: The item, or null for the plan.

approvalId.description: The approval row of an owner decision.

conservativeExpectancyR.description: Conservative expectancy in R, or null.

advisoryNote.description: A model's figure, labelled advisory, or null.

PlanEvidenceView.description: The evidence of a ticket, with its limits.

report.description: The curves and groups of this plan.

state.description: The ticket state; null for a rejected candidate, which is not a ticket.

nextStates.description: States the ticket may move to; empty for a rejected candidate.

attempt.description: 1 for the first attempt of the planned session.

planKey.description: The plan key when a plan was published.

failedGate.description: The gate that blocked, or null.

reviewCutoff.description: After this an owner approval or modification is refused; undecided tickets lapse.

state.description: draft, published, inreview, approved, rejected, lapsed, armed or expired.

nextStates.description: The states the plan may move to.

provisional.description: Whether cells were not yet paper-proven.

items.description: The candidates; empty in a list.

history.description: The trail, oldest first; empty in a list.

PlanView.description: A plan as the API shows it (P7-03, ADR 0083): header, current state, the sentences it carries as data, and for one plan the tickets and the trail.

PortfolioHistory.description:
The value history of a scope (all accounts that count in totals, one account, one bucket). `Points` are in date order at `Resolution` (`day`, `week` or `month`: the last trading day of the period); `Value` is what the
lots held that day were worth at that day's close (adjusted for splits and bonuses), `Invested` what they cost, `BenchmarkValue` the same cash flows in the benchmark index, `Nav` and `BenchmarkNav` unit values starting at 100
that cash flows do not move. `Coverage` says how many open holdings have price history; `Partial` is true when anything is left out (holdings without bars, history that starts late). `MaxDrawdown` / `BenchmarkMaxDrawdown`: the largest
fall of the NAV measured within the requested range (`Pct` 12.5 = fell 12.5 %; the peak must lie inside the range too) between the peak on `From` and the low on `To`, daily, whatever the resolution; `RangeFrom` and `RangeTo` are the first and
the last day of that range as returned (null when there is no point). `FirstDate` is the first day of the whole history (before the range is cut). `LastPriceAt` is set when the last point is today's live one: the time of the newest price in it.

PortfolioInput.description: The portfolio configuration to change. Every field that is left out (null) keeps the account's current value, on update. DefaultBucket: the name of the bucket imports go to — a custom bucket's name; an empty string "" (or the name of the account's own "{account name} · Portfolio" bucket) selects the account's own default bucket; null or omitted keeps the current choice. IncludeInTotals: true or false; null keeps it. At account creation, omitted means the account's own bucket and true. The automatic holdings refresh: RefreshMode "off" or "daily"; RefreshDailyTimeIst "HH:mm" (India time); left out keeps the current value (a new account: off, 16:00). FirstImportDate (not in the future, not before 1990-01-01) is the date the first import gives holdings without a date of their own. FirstImport is honoured only when updating the portfolio settings of an account (it is ignored at account creation): see FirstImportInput.

PortfolioNotice.description: One notice of the Portfolio module for the top-bar bell. `Kind` is `price_alert_triggered` (`Severity` warn; `AlertId` and `InstrumentId` set), `actions_need_decision` (info) or - since ADR 0027 - an attention item: `reconnect_dhan`, `sync_failing`, `holdings_need_review`, `trades_unexplained`, `dividends_pending`, `securities_unmatched` or `rows_dropped` (`Severity` error, warning or info; `AccountId` set). `Id` is stable and, for an attention item, includes its situation, so a changed situation is a new item and the bell keeps what was read by id. Since ADR 0027 every notice also has a `Title`, at most two `Actions` (a route to open or an existing endpoint to call), `Since` (when it was first seen; null for a notice derived on read that is not remembered - `actions_need_decision` - whose id already changes with the India date, so a client that keys read state on id and since sees the same key on every poll) and `Resolved`: an attention item whose condition stopped holding is kept for 24 hours with `Resolved` true and then dropped; resolved items are not counted in the badge. `At` is kept as it was (the time of the event, or `Since` for an attention item).

PortfolioSaved.description: The answer of saving the portfolio settings: the account as saved and what the first import did (always present; see FirstImportView).

PortfolioSettingsView.description:
Portfolio configuration. DefaultBucket is the name of the bucket imports go to (the account's own default bucket unless a custom bucket was chosen);
AutoBucketName is the name of the account's own default bucket ("{account name} · Portfolio") — the one that exists, or, while the account has none yet,
the name it would get now (with a numeric suffix when the plain name is taken); it is chosen for real when the role is switched on.
The holdings refresh by themselves according to RefreshMode: "off" (default) or "daily" (once a day from RefreshDailyTimeIst, "HH:mm" India time, default 16:00;
the time is kept while the mode is off). FirstImportDate is the date holdings get when they are imported for the first time without a date of their own
(2025-01-01 until the owner chooses another). HasHoldings is true once the account has any holding; the first import has happened then and
FirstImportDate no longer affects existing holdings (ADR 0013).

PortfolioTrackResult.description: What a track action did. `Requested` distinct master-list instruments were asked to be tracked, `Added` of them are newly tracked (or tracked again), `AlreadyTracked` were; `NotInMaster` open holdings in scope are not in the instrument master (nothing to track), `Retired` instruments are no longer listed and were skipped. `TotalTracked` is the number tracked now. No job is started: `Hint` says the next Update data builds the bars.

PreviewCsvFilesRequest.description: The files to preview: names from the folder listing, at most int PreviewCsvFilesHandler.MaxFiles.

PreviewRow.description:
A holding Dhan reports, for the first import in the portfolio settings. Key identifies it in the import request (the ISIN, otherwise "securityId:EXCHANGE").
Mapped is false when it is not in the instrument master. AlreadyImported: the account has the holding (open) already.
SuggestedDate is the date to pre-fill: the first import date, or the oldest lot's date of an already imported holding.

PriceAlertInput.description: A new price alert: the master-list share or ETF, `Direction``at_or_below|at_or_above`, the `Level` in rupees (above 0, at most 10,000,000, at most 4 decimals) and an optional plain-text `Note` of at most 200 characters.

PriceAlertPage.description: One page of alerts, newest first (`Total` counts all matches). `ActiveCount` of `ActiveLimit` alerts are active, whatever the filter.

PriceAlertView.description:
A price alert. `Status` is `active`, `triggered` (with `TriggeredAt` and `TriggerPrice`, the last price of the tick that hit the level) or `cancelled`. It is checked on the last price of each quotes tick only (every 5 minutes while the market
is open): a spike between two ticks is not seen.

PricesAsOf.description: The oldest and the newest time of the prices of the open holdings (null when none has a priced time).

items.description:
The latest known price of an instrument: `lastPrice` at `priceAt` (the time of the exchange's tick for `live`, the time of the quote for `quote`, the time of the sync for `sync`; UTC) and where it came from:
`live` (the live feed), `quote` (the 5-minute quote poll) or `sync` (the broker's holdings list). The same values as `lastPrice`, `priceAt` and `priceSource` of the holdings list. An older price never follows a newer one
for the same instrument; a client that gets one anyway ignores it.

PricesChanged.description:
Hub event `pricesChanged`: the prices that changed for the instruments the connection follows since the last message sent to it (the first messages after `Subscribe` carry all of them). At most one burst a second;
at most 500 instruments and 32 KB per message (a larger change comes as several messages with the same `asOf`). `asOf` is the server's time when it read the prices (UTC).

code.description: Stable machine-readable error code, e.g. auth.invalid_credentials, auth.locked, auth.session_expired, auth.csrf_invalid, auth.step_up_required, accounts.not_found, accounts.invalid (field errors in "errors"), accounts.conflict, accounts.app_not_configured, accounts.broker_error (502), accounts.connect_mismatch, accounts.consent_limit (429), accounts.connect_expired, accounts.connect_cancelled, portfolio.not_connected, portfolio.sync_running, portfolio.confirmation_required and portfolio.confirmation_stale (409, with listedHoldings, openHoldings and wouldClose), portfolio.conflict (409), portfolio.invalid, portfolio.not_found, portfolio.lot_from_trade (409), portfolio.preview_stale (409, with report), services.not_found (404), services.invalid (400, with issues), services.revision_changed (409), services.already_running (409), services.read_only (409).

retryAfterSeconds.description: Present on auth.locked, auth.rate_limited and accounts.consent_limit: seconds until a new attempt may succeed.

openHoldings.description: Present on portfolio.confirmation_required and portfolio.confirmation_stale: how many holdings the account has open.

listedHoldings.description: Present on portfolio.confirmation_required and portfolio.confirmation_stale: how many holdings Dhan listed.

issues.description: Present on services.invalid: every error of the refused schedule - the service it is about (serviceId; absent for the service of the request), the field (a dotted path like the request, e.g. schedule.time, retries, parameters.x), severity (error), a stable code and the text.

report.description: Present on portfolio.preview_stale: the fresh preview of the file, in the shape of the response of POST /api/portfolio/trades/preview (TradePreviewReport).

wouldClose.description: Present on portfolio.confirmation_required: how many of them the sync would close because Dhan no longer lists them.

QualityBucketRow.description: A bucket stored and recomputed side by side; `fields` name what differs (open, high, low, close, volume, bars) or `missing` / `unexpected`; `stored` or `recomputed` is null when there is none.

QualityBucketValues.description: The values of a bucket: open, high, low, close, volume and the number of 1-minute bars in it.

QualityBuckets.description:
The stored and the recomputed buckets of the window, computed when asked (`computedAt`), so they show the state now, whatever the last run saw. `total` and `differences` count all buckets of the
request's timeframe filter; `items` are cut at 2000 (`truncated`); with `differencesOnly` only the differing ones are listed.

QualityCheckResults.description: The checks of one instrument as the last run found them (without the long lists, which the detail gives separately).

QualityCheckStatuses.description: The status of each check of an instrument: pass · warning · fail · notAvailable (`officialDaily`).

QualityCounts.description:
The current results over the tracked instruments that have bars: how many there are (`tracked`), how many were `checked` (have a result), the counts by result, `notChecked`, and the mean score
of the results (null before the first run). The current result of an instrument is the one of the latest run that checked it.

QualityGateView.description:
The gate for the nightly plan (fail-closed). `blocked`: no run yet, the last run over every instrument failed, or more than `maxFailedPercent` of the checked instruments fail;
`ok`: not blocked and no instrument fails; `reasons` says why it is not ok. Instruments that fail individually are skipped by the scan whatever the gate says.

QualityInstrumentDetail.description:
One instrument's quality: the current result (`status` pass · warning · fail · notChecked, `score`, `checks` from the run `runId` at `checkedAt`), the missing minutes of that run
and the stored-vs-recomputed buckets as they are now.

QualityInstrumentRow.description:
An instrument in the quality table. `status`: pass · warning · fail · notChecked (never checked). `coverage` is the share of the expected minutes that are stored (percent); `aggregates` gives the status
of each timeframe (5m … 1M); `checks` the status of each check; `issues` says in words what is wrong; `source`: csv · dhan · mixed.

QualityMissing.description: The missing minutes of the window: `total` of them, and the first `items` (at most 500; `truncated` when there are more).

QualityOverview.description:
What the Data quality screen shows above the table: `lastRun` (the latest run over every instrument, null before the first), the `counts` of the current results with the mean `score`,
the `gate`, the `window`, the limits in force (`spikeMultiple`, `maxMissingPercent`) and `pendingCorporateActions`: the suggested splits and bonus issues waiting for the owner (ADR 0017 §5).

QualityPhase.description:
The quality phase of a data job (P1-14a): `Done` of `Total` are instruments checked. `RunId` is the quality run it recorded
(`/api/data/quality/runs`); `Passed`, `Warned` and `Failed` count the instruments by result so far. Part of the API (the job's
`quality` block, present only when the job asked for the step).

QualityRunView.description:
One run of the data quality checks. `trigger`: manual · daily (the scheduled end-of-day run) · after_job (a data job the owner started with the quality step). `status`: running · succeeded · failed.
`instruments` is how many the run checks, `passed`, `warned` and `failed` how many it has checked so far with that result; `score` is the mean (0–100, once it ended).
`instrumentId` is set when the run checked one instrument only (a fix action); `jobId` is the data job it belongs to.

QualityWindowView.description: The window of the checks: how many closed sessions, from which date to which (the ones a run started now would look at).

RefreshRunView.description: One refresh run. `trigger`: manual · daily · forced; `status`: running · succeeded · unchanged · failed; `phase` (while running): downloading · parsing · enriching · saving.

RefreshStarted.description: The refresh that was registered; follow it with `GET /api/instruments/refresh/status`.

RefreshStatusView.description: Where the master list stands: the refresh in progress (if any), the last finished one, the automatic schedule and how many instruments are active.

RemoveMembersInput.description: Instruments to remove from a basket (1 to 500; repeats count once).

RemoveMembersResult.description: What a removal did: `removed` were members, `notMembers` were not. Untracking never happens. `memberCount` = members now.

ReportKpisView.description: The headline figures of the out-of-sample evidence; a figure that is not finite is null.

ReportRunView.description: What was tested: the strategy version, the method, the window and the universe (spec P5-06).

ReportUploadForm.description:
The multipart form of the report preview and import, for the API contract only (the request is read by ReportUploads). `AccountId` is the account, `Files` the downloaded reports (one or more; CSV, XLS or XLSX). `Choices` is a JSON array of
`{name, holdingId | instrumentId | isin, remember}`: what scrip names of a transaction report mean. For the import also `Digests` (a JSON array with the preview's digest, or null, for each file in order), `Rebuild` (whether to rebuild the lots of
trade files, default true) and `AcceptOtherAccount` (a JSON array of the indexes, from 0, of the files to import although the report is for another client code).

ReportWarningView.description: A caution derived from the report's own numbers. It never changes the outcome.

ResolveInput.description: Pasted tickers, canonical symbols (`NSE:RELIANCE`) or ISINs, up to 5,000 entries.

ResolveResult.description:
The outcome of looking up a pasted list. `entries` counts the non-blank entries, `duplicates` those collapsed because an earlier entry
was the same text or named the same instrument. Entries that match nothing are never guessed: they are listed in `unmatched`.

ResolvedInstrument.description: An entry that named an instrument. `term` is the entry as typed (the first one when several name the same instrument); `tracked` = tracked now; `retired` = cannot be newly tracked.

ReturnsView.description: The profit/loss figures that every holding row, lot row and summary carries.

RiskProfileInput.description: The values of a risk profile to create or to replace an existing one with. Every value is required.

RobustnessView.description: The robustness block of a result (spec P5-05, ADR 0062). It does not change the verdict; every part that cannot be computed is null or says why.

RolesInput.description: Roles to switch; a role that is left out stays as it is.

SanityCheck.description: Bar sanity: low ≤ open and close ≤ high, prices positive and finite, volume not negative. `examples` holds the first few bad bars.

SchedulePreview.description: The dry run of a schedule: the findings (errors and warnings), the next three starts after now (empty when the schedule has errors or follows another service) and the schedule in words.

ScheduleSpec.description:
A Schedule as text: what the API sends and receives and what the database stores (JSON). `type` is daily · weekly · after · window · interval · continuous; times are
`HH:mm` India time; `days` are mon … sun; `weekday` is one of them; `after` is a service id. Fields that do not belong to the type are left out (null).

SecretStatusView.description: Whether one of the owner's Dhan secrets is stored (encrypted) and when it last changed. Name is the request field name ("apiKey", "apiSecret"). The value itself is never returned.

SecretsInput.description:
The Dhan API key and secret, write-only (app_id / app_secret). Surrounding spaces are
removed; the values are stored encrypted and never returned.

SensitivityView.description: The parameter sensitivity (spec P5-05): the exit and timeframe every point used, the base and the parameters.

ServiceIssueView.description: A finding of the schedule checks. `severity`: error (blocks saving) · warning. `field` is a dotted path like the request (schedule.time, retries, parameters.x); `relatedServiceId` names the other service of a finding that involves two.

ServiceList.description: Every service: the registered ones in screen order, then the read-only entries.

ServiceLiveView.description:
What a service that another process runs (the live feed) says about itself, from that process's heartbeat: `state` is its state word (connected · idle · connecting · reconnecting · closed · paused · no_token · token_refused · flapping ·
stopped · not_running when it reports nothing), `connected` whether it holds a connection, `subscribed` the instruments it carries, `lastTickAt` the time of the last price, `ticksPerSecond` its rate, `lastSeenAt` the
time of the heartbeat (null when it has never reported) and `summary` the one line the card shows.

ServiceNotice.description: A failure to tell the owner of (the bell). `id` is `service:failed:{serviceId}:{yyyy-MM-dd}` (the India date of the failed run): one notice per service per day, with the text and time of the latest failure. `kind` is service_failed; `severity` error.

ServiceRunPage.description: A page of runs, newest first. At most the latest int ServiceRunLimits.MaxShown runs of a service are shown; `total` counts those.

ServiceRunView.description:
One run (or attempt) of a service. `trigger`: scheduled · catch_up · after · manual. `status`: running · succeeded · failed · skipped; `queued` only in the answer to Run now for a service that another process runs (the live feed):
the request was accepted and the record does not exist yet (`id` is empty). `dataJobId` links the data job a run started.

ServiceScheduleInput.description:
The body of a schedule save or preview: everything the dialog sets, all of it required (a body that leaves a field out is a 400, so a missing switch is never read as "off"). `parameters` are the values by name
(those left out keep the schema's default); `revision` is the one read with the service (0 for a service that has no stored choices yet, also the default) and is only checked by a save.

ServiceStatus.description:
A background process by its heartbeat. `isAlive`: it reported within the last 60 seconds. `state`: what it says about itself (the feed: connected, idle, closed, paused, …; `stopped` in the last beat of a process that was told
to stop on purpose, which does not make the system unhealthy for ten minutes); null for a process that only says it is alive (the worker).

ServiceView.description:
A service on the Services screen (ADR 0018). `status`: healthy · running · failed (its latest run failed) · paused. `schedule` is the stored form (`scheduleWords` says it in words);
`allowedScheduleTypes` are the types the owner may choose; `isDefault` says the choices are the definition's defaults; `lastRun` is the latest run of any kind, `nextRun` the next
scheduled start (null when paused, when it follows another service, is always up or has no day ahead). `revision` is sent back with a save (0 until the first save or seed). A `readOnly`
entry is set elsewhere (`manageUrl`) and refuses writes. `live` is only given for a service that another process runs (the live feed): what its heartbeat says; its `status` is then derived from the stored row, the
